Chapter 5. A Turbulent Era

Two hundred years have passed in the blink of an eye.

Daeva who have abandoned the fight and those who still endure alike feel their hopes slowly fading.

I. Introduction

No other organization on Atreia has accomplished more in the field of life modification than the Lepharists.
As a senior researcher, I am pleased to have contributed to the work of the Lepharists over the centuries. I dedicate this work to the great Lephar himself, and to the current head of our order.



II. About Krao

- Krao is a transparent, high-strength mineral formed deep below the crust under ultra-high pressure, and relatively easy to obtain due to its abundant reserves.- Krao was mainly used as a raw material for forging armor and was not utilized as a precious metal or for other kinds of crafting. It was not until 200 years, with the discovery of <QK>Red Krao</>, that it started being recognized for its special properties.
- 200 years ago, following the establishment of a Drana cultivation complex in Verteron by the Ishtar Legion, soil exposed to Drana began to undergo metamorphic reactions.
- <QK>Red Krao</> discovered in the Drana Fields was found to be capable of deflecting impacts entirely rather than absorbing them.
- Some Lepharist researchers (hereafter referred to as Krao Researchers) have set up laboratories in natural caves where Krao veins are found, and continue to study the new mutations.

III. Overview of Krao Experiments

- Research into ancient mutant life has been successful in finding methods of cutting off an organism from the Odyle cycle in order to enhance its inherent unique abilities.

- Krao Researchers have undertaken mutant adaptation experiments in which they gradually increase the content of Drana under conditions of extreme Odyle deprivation. In nature, Daeva exposed to Drana for long periods of time are able to adapt without dying.
- In light of this, the researchers conducted a series of experiments, starting with Krao transplants and ending with direct Drana infusions.

IV. Classification of Krao Test Subjects

- Experiment (Phase 1)

After the adaptation period following the implantation of Krao crystals, the skin's strength increased and granulation occurred at the extremities of the body. The mutant maintains an appearance similar to the human form that served as its mold, while gaining a magnetic field and aerial movement capabilities.
However, it retains little cognitive ability, and is therefore incapable of being taught.

- Experiment (Phase 2)

While essentially the same as Phase 1, rejections that occurred after gene transplantation between other organisms were significantly reduced.
Body enhancement experiments were accelerated by transplanting parts from different organisms, and the number of subjects that maintained a stable half-human appearance increased. Though higher cognitive abilities were present compared to Phase 1, they were merely fragmented conscious responses, and most significantly, dissociative personalities were widely observed.
Some subjects were also observed referring the themselves with the plural "we".
This phenomenon is discussed further in the <QK>Berk</> entry.

V. Berk

<QK>Berk</> is defined as a metallic weapon based on an organic organism. Krao experimental subjects are fully crystallized, with the enhanced skin tissue within their human body repeatedly undergoing division and synthesis.
Those Krao who go through the repeated destruction and growth of their own Krao particles are classified as Berk. These Berks can move along an orbit in a configuration that encircles a Krao Orb core.
Reaction experiments revealed that, despite being inorganic, neuroactive substances are transmitted to the Krao particles.
Berks utilize surrounding Krao minerals to generate enough thermal energy per individual to match a small nuclear reactor.
They are also the only test subjects to exhibit high levels of intelligence and are expected to be viable as anti-personnel weapons when equipped with guidance devices.
However, they too have been observed to exhibit multiple personalities, and will therefore require careful management.

This truth will be hidden from future generations.

Chapter 2: The Collapse of the Tower
It all began with the <QK>Collapse</>.
The endless war between the Elyos and the Asmodians and the ever-growing Abyss drained Odyle at an alarming rate.
Consequently, the Tower of Eternity began to crumble.
The Tower of Eternity, the very source of Daevahood, faltered— and so too did the power of the Daeva.

The Balaur swept across Poeta and Verteron with terrifying speed.
Then came <QK>Ishtar</>, leading grotesque legions resembling no living creature found on Atreia.
Elyos Daeva joined forces to fight back, only to fall one by one, having been greatly weakened.

Before long, it was revealed that those hideous legions were once our kin, fallen victim to Ishtar's experiments.
Past comrades, family, lovers, all turned into <QK>Sura</>, weapons of the Balaur. Yet we had no choice but to raise our blades against them.
There was no time for grief. Only the despair of battle.

Then the day came.
A thunderous roar shook the world and tremors split the sky.
Shards of the great Tower rained down across the land. It was as if a divine will had declared the end of an era.

The following day, and the one after... the world fell eerily silent.
Even the Balaur halted their advance. Why?

Was it a sign?
A harbinger of a new age?

Following the collapse of the Tower,
the Empyrean Lords feared Atreia would soon fall entirely to the Balaur.
But opinions diverged even among themselves.
As signs of Ishtar's army stirring grew more frequent, the Empyrean Lords made their final decision.


Chapter 3: The Bulwark Is Raised
Ariel, the highest among the Empyrean Lords, took the lead, with Kaisinel and Yustiel by her side.
Together, they resolved to raise a great <QK>bulwark at the edge of the Eltnen Desert</> to halt the Balaur advance.
No decision could have been more painful.

When the Bulwark rose, it was as if a storm scoured the land.
All life, all that the Daeva had built, vanished into the sands of the Eracus Desert.

The Empyrean Lords, having exhausted their strength, suffered extinction or otherwise faded beyond our reach.

Clinging to our final hope, we passed through the area of the rising Bulwark into Interdica.
Elysium itself was being relocated above our heads.
It was a strange sight. Beyond the wall were dark clouds, but here, where I stand—radiant light.
The people left behind would be forgiven for seeing this as the day the world ended.

Surely, if the world were ever to end, it would look like this:
the complete fall of the Tower, the ruin of Atreia, being engulfed by the Abyss.

Ah, the gate will soon be closed.
To think—Elysea divided in two... Will our world ever be whole again?

When the storm settles, the Bulwark will be revealed.
A wall hidden within a sandstorm. A wall so vast the eye cannot fully comprehend it. The edge of the world.

Like the final command of the Empyrean Lords, all things scatter, and the world stands still before the closed gate.
I pray my testimony may reach the edge of the world beyond that Bulwark.
And may you, who read this, understand the truth, and reclaim what it means to be a Daeva.

You who behold this document: locate the Bulwark!
Find the path towards making Atreia whole again!

<Ruins of the Ancient City of Ru>
The city of Ru prospered during the golden age before the Great Catastrophe, when all Daeva lived together in peace. Today, the Shuriman Expedition tirelessly searches the Abyss for the hidden entrance to this lost city.

<Ruins of the Ruhn Sanctuary>
Originally built as a mausoleum for the Ruhn elite, the Ruhn Sanctuary stood as a symbol of their power and became the resting place of countless cultural treasures.

Over time, ordinary Ruhn began entering the sanctuary as well. Fearing that this would diminish their authority, the elite constructed an elaborate labyrinth to keep intruders out. Its intricate passages also made it an ideal vault for precious artifacts, causing even greater riches to be entombed within.

Among these treasures lie not only gold and silver, but also invaluable Ruhn knowledge, including techniques for harnessing Ydgel energy.

After learning of these hidden relics, a band of Shugo and Shulak tomb raiders launched an ambitious expedition to seize the lost legacy of the Ruhn.

<Runadium Ruins>
The dwelling of Grendal Eronale, a witch cursed by the Danuar.

Once a subterranean cavern overflowing with powerful Ydyle energy, it was later transformed into a sanctuary where Danuar mages gathered to study and hone their magical arts.

<Runatorium Ruins>
The Runatorium was a vast circular arena where the Ruhn staged battles between creatures corrupted by Ydyle for their own amusement.

One such creature, driven mad by the torment of its corruption, began devouring the foes it defeated. With every victim it consumed, it absorbed more Ide and grew even stronger.

Yet this newfound power only intensified its corruption. Its flesh twisted into an even more grotesque form until, in time, the creature lost all sense of self, becoming nothing more than a bloodthirsty beast driven by an insatiable urge to slaughter.

<Site of the Hall of Knowledge>
Once a grand library preserving ancient Ruhn knowledge of Ydyle, Ydylium, and Ydgel, the library was desecrated by Dragon Lord Beritra and transformed into a storage facility for Ydgel and a prison for experimental subjects.

While searching for traces of Ydgel, Beritra's intelligence forces discovered both the Hall and hidden Ydgel reserves beneath Sillus Fortress. They converted the site into a laboratory for biological experimentation.

Even now, the scars of torture and brutality remain etched into its walls.

After the Last War, those left outside the Bulwark were forced to endure Odyle shortages and unexplained mutations. Fear soon took hold, and anyone who showed signs of mutation was branded a Karas. Many who had only just begun to transform were banished or buried alive before they even understood what was happening.

Only the Three Sisters of Fate were able to restore order in this age of chaos. Living in seclusion within the Moslan Forest, they offered refuge to fleeing Karas and discovered a way to halt the progression of the Karas mutation through the use of petrification magic.

Those whose mutations were halted concealed the remaining signs beneath heavy garments and made their home deep within the forest alongside the Three Sisters. Thus, the group known as the Nornir was born.

The Three Sisters taught the Nornir magic and divination so they could survive beyond the Bulwark. To the Nornir, the Three Sisters were both saviors and mentors. Without their guidance, Altgard would have fallen into even greater devastation and despair.

With deep remorse for failing to trust my teacher, and with profound respect for the achievements of the Three Sisters, I dedicate this book to Urd, Verdandi, and Skuld, the Three Sisters of Fate.

From the days of the Elyos-Asmodian War, Reda has fought unceasingly on the front lines for the Elyos. Her commanding presence and powerful magical ability were more than enough to rally allies on the battlefield.
A peer to the legendary Elyos hero Akarios, Reda eventually swore the <QK>Illusion Covenant</> with Kaisinel.
The content of a covenant with an Empyrean Lord is known only to the one who receives it, and the details of that made by Reda remains undisclosed.

After the Great Catastrophe, the Empyrean Lords split into two factions: the Elyos and Asmodians. Neither side held much hope for Atreia's future.
A few still quietly dreamed of restoring ancient Atreia, a unified land where Elyos and Asmodians would once again live as one people.
But the threat of Odyle's extinction was too pressing for any Lord to express such ideals openly.
To the Empyrean Lords, choosing which side should survive was not a question of morality or justice. Both were equally deserving.

<QK>Chapter 1: How the Ancients Saw Odyle</>
Deliberating on Odyle, the essence of all life that encompasses Atreia, is a delicate matter. Even in ancient times, the power of Odyle over life was common knowledge. The ancients believed all things arose from union with Odyle, though they often treated it as no more than an alchemical ingredient. Their blind faith in Odyle's power led them to pursue the extraction of high-purity Odyle and the creation of new life.

Ancient alchemists mistakenly believed they were omnipotent beings who could control Odyle's power, and were determined to prove themselves. Consequently, the study of Odyle went astray, and ancient alchemy headed down a path of corruption. It is without question that they made the wrong choices, not the least because Odyle is not simply a material that makes up life.

<QK>Chapter 2: What is Odyle?</>
Today's definition of Odyle is not so different from that of the ancients, save for the crucial difference of recognizing Odyle energy not as simply the material source of life but as a spiritual principle. This viewpoint follows the enlightenment of Lumiel, the Empyrean Lord of Wisdom. Lumiel's definition is regarded as closest to the essence of Odyle and advanced the understandings of Odylogy significantly.

Scholars seeking to unravel the mysteries of Odyle have moved beyond traditional materialist thought, venturing into uncharted realms concerning life and the mind. This approach has proven valid following the confirmation that Odyle and life interact to keep Atreia in harmonious balance.

<QK>Chapter 3: The Power Within Odyle</>
Many examples can be presented to illustrate how Odyle affects life. These relate to the power inherent in Odyle. One well-known case is the "Ascension" of humans into Daeva through Odyle's special influence, and the fact that Kibelisks are placed in areas emitting the purest form of Odyle.

Conversely, when Odyle is lacking, forests become barren and deserts spread. Some claim that Balaur within the Abyss have mentally and physically degenerated after excessive exposure to Odyle. These are key examples of how an imbalance of Odyle in either direction can alter life. Still, the fundamental question of what Odyle's power truly is remains unresolved.

<QK>Chapter 4: The Ability to Harness Odyle</>
The ability to harness Odyle seems to be innate. Thus, "How does one become skilled in using Odyle's power?" is not really the right question. Most people who can manipulate Odyle discovered their gift at some point in life. It might have been triggered by chance or a dream, where they awoke compelled by a mysterious force to morph substances with Odyle. Whatever the cause, Daeva today make broad use of Odyle's power, a talent that is highly valued.

<QK>Chapter 5: Applications of Odylogy</>
This chapter briefly introduces practical uses of Odylogy. Odyle's applications in healing and resurrection—likely achieved through spiritual effects—are not yet fully understood. Odyle also serves as an ingredient in the morphing of substances in all crafts except cooking.

Odyle can appear as powder, crystals, shards, or in its raw form. The purer it is, the more valuable it is for professional crafting. Extracting Odyle requires mastery of Odyle-extraction techniques. This can be purchased with Kina up to a certain level, but Daeva aiming higher must pass a promotion exam.

<QK>Chapter 6: On Stigma Crystals</>
Stigma Crystals, known to embody part of Odyle's energy, are closely linked to Odyle. During the Millennium War, the Great Catastrophe, and the Elyos-Asmodian War in the Abyss, countless Daeva perished. Though their bodies were destroyed, their spirits roamed Atreia, merged with Odyle, and crystallized for reasons unknown, resulting in Stigma Crystals.

Researchers have long focused on how the spiritual essences of deceased Daeva merged with Odyle as it is viewed as a vital key to understanding how Odyle influences life. Despite this, research remains at a standstill, though there is good reason to hope that future breakthroughs in Odylogy will arise from the study of Stigma Crystals.

Today, I will explain the difference between the often confused concepts of <QK>Fafnite</> and <QK>Fafnium</>.

<QK>What is Fafnite?</>

Fafnite is a blue gemstone found in the Gribade Highlands of Altgard.
It is a metamorphic rock formed long ago under the intense heat and pressure of the Gribade volcanic field. Its naturally deep blue color has made it highly prized as a gemstone. Mining began in earnest about 180 years ago after it drew the attention of Dragon Lord Fafnir. Today, its trade is a major source of income for the Shulak of the Gribade region.

Strictly speaking, it is technically incorrect to call this blue gemstone "Fafnite" unless it has been imbued with a soul through the beautiful and intricate process made possible only by the power of Dragon Lord Fafnir. However, over time, the name "Fafnite" has come to refer to the gemstone regardless of whether it contains a soul.

<QK>What is Fafnium?</>

Fafnium is a device that allows anyone to imbue Fafnite with a soul, replicating the power once exclusive to Dragon Lord Fafnir.

When properly installed and activated, a Fafnium device absorbs the souls of nearby humans or Daeva. Fafnium devices exist in many sizes, ranging from compact mechanisms suitable for concealed traps to massive installations capable of harvesting every soul within a wide area.

<QK>Activating Fafnite and Fafnium</>

A single Fafnium device can absorb multiple souls, making it a devastating weapon of mass destruction.

If a particularly strong-willed Daeva resists the effects of Fafnium, simply rendering them unconscious is usually sufficient.

Once imbued, Fafnite serves as a medium through which the abilities of the captured soul can be harnessed. Worn as an accessory or fused directly into the body, it can enhance physical abilities or grant access to the original owner's powers.

However, Fafnite contains the power of Fafnir himself. Never attempt to wield that power recklessly. Those who fail to master it risk horrific bodily mutations, or worse, having their very bodies consumed and taken over by the Fafnite.

I. Overview

Odyle is the primordial energy that empowers the Daeva and sustains the barrier protecting Atreia.

Since the Great Catastrophe, Odyle reserves have diminished at an alarming rate, posing an existential threat to the world. In response, scholars have devoted themselves to the study of Odyle, developing methods to classify its natural forms, extract it from the environment, and preserve it for future use.

II. Forms of Odyle

<QK>Odylium</>

A crystalline mineral formed when Odyle fuses with natural ores. Even those unable to wield Odyle directly can harness its power through refined Odylium, making it one of Atreia's most valuable resources. It is found primarily in Elysea and is highly prized by the Krall.

<QK>Odylla</>

A rare herb native to Asmodae that draws the energy required for its growth from atmospheric Odyle. Because Odyle is present throughout its biological structure, it can be refined into a concentrated liquid using purification techniques pioneered by the Mau. The Skurv are also renowned for their expertise in cultivating Odylla.

<QK>Odyllon</>

A species of tree genetically engineered to store exceptionally dense Odyle energy for extraction. Its fruit possesses potent psychoactive properties and is commonly fermented into liquor.

<QK>Odyle Shard</>

A solid cluster of microscopic crystals that naturally exhibits the properties of Odyle. Thanks to its unique characteristics, it serves as a fundamental medium in countless applications throughout Atreia. Odyle Shards are notably the primary material used to restore the Collapsed Verteron Barrier Tower.

III. Odyle Procurement

<QK>Obelisk</>

A device created by the Empyrean Lord Kaisinel and his Cavaliers during the ancient Battle of Inggison. Embedded with fragments of the AION Tower, it generates Odyle and creates a localized field of its energy wherever it is erected.

<QK>Artificial Odyle Generator</>

An ancient Odyle circulation device developed by the Empyrean Lord Lumiel in Asmodae. It harvests trace amounts of Odyle from the surrounding environment, creating a localized field of Odyle around itself.

<QK>Odyle Collector</>

A device developed by the Creion by combining the principles of the Obelisk and the Artificial Odyle Generator. It can detect trace amounts of Odyle in the atmosphere and within living organisms, extracting them as concentrated ore fragments. However, its delicate filtration system is highly susceptible to failure.

IV. Odyle Storage

Much of the knowledge surrounding Odyle storage was lost during the Last War, and no reliable method of preserving large quantities has since been rediscovered.

In ancient times, highly concentrated Odyle was preserved and distributed in the form of Odyle Jelly, though the recipes required to produce it have become exceedingly rare.

In recent years, researchers have turned their attention to Drana-adapted organisms in the hope of developing alternative methods for storing and producing Odyle.

One day, a debate broke out during a gathering of Kaisinel's envoys.
The discussion pertained to whether they should keep or do away with Kaisinel's spell related to the "Resurrection of Spirits," which they interpreted as Scarlotus.
Spirits, being metaphysical, do not belong to the material world. Like Odyle, they are formless, closer to the essence of nature formed through elemental fusion.
The envoys' translation of Scarlotus described a <QK>resurrection ritual for souls</> based on the idea that "Spirits do not experience death and instead circulate endlessly—just like the Daeva."
The spell can be summarized as follows:
A being is divided into three parts—mind, body, and soul. Then, when a soul nears extinction, it is replaced with a Spirit. A lifeform infused with the soul of a Spirit possesses no self-awareness but, having gained a powerful soul, may serve as a summoned creature of elemental nature.

Most envoys agreed the spell could be easily abused. It was ultimately decided that it would never be disclosed to the public but instead classified as a sealed tome of the Illusion tier.
However, the Illusion Legion, eager to create an undying army to wield against the Asmodians, made contact with Typhlos, who subsequently volunteered to test the spell himself.

The result is as history remembers.
To this day, an Elysea village remains closed to all civilian Daeva.

Some Empyrean Lords held Kaisinel accountable for the incident, but he dismissed the accusation, stating that those who could not see the essence of nature even with open eyes were truly blind, and that it was not his responsibility to awaken the dull-witted.

Daeva of today no longer fear the Dredgion, despite knowing that an encounter with one would almost certainly mean death and rebirth.
Even now, I am still haunted by nightmares of my first encounter with such a behemoth of the skies. Many years have passed, yet the memory remains as vivid as the day it happened.

The first Dredgion appeared without warning. There were no signs of its approach, only the unsettling silence of the Balaur. For months, fortress assaults ceased, artifacts went untouched, and even our messengers reported little resistance.
In that uneasy calm, we grew distracted by our struggle for dominance over the Elyos in Reshanta, failing to notice the Balaur's quiet, unnatural stillness. Then, amid a fierce battle at Sulfur Tree Island, a strange and overwhelming energy surged from Reshanta's Eye.

We knew at once it was not Odyle energy. It filled us with an instinctive dread that needed no explanation. Without a word, Archons and Guardians alike ceased their fighting and turned toward the Eye. What had been a distant speck became a colossal, suffocating presence in an instant.

Instinct told me it was Balaur in origin. Fear seized me, along with an overwhelming urge to flee, yet I forced myself to stand my ground despite knowing victory was impossible.

"It is the Balaur! Halt its advance!" our commander shouted.

We surged toward the Dredgion. The Guardians, too, regained their resolve and joined the charge. But as we closed in, the vanguard began to fall like insects as red and blue beams carved through the sky.

I was struck and frozen by a blue ray, while my comrades fell to burning red light, their wings still unfurled as they vanished midair. The Guardian forces mirrored our fate on the opposite flank. Countless white wings blossomed and were extinguished in an instant. A single graze from the red beams was enough to snuff out life.

The high commander ordered a retreat, but the Dredgion gave us no chance to withdraw. Beams poured from every direction. There was no path to escape. That first encounter ended in nothing but terror and devastation for both Asmodians and Elyos alike.

Beyond the physical losses, an even deeper wound remained, the knowledge that an enemy beyond our power had revealed itself. We reported the Dredgion's appearance to the Supreme Commander, yet no strategy could be formed against such an unknown threat. For a long time after, fear followed every flight into battle, though the Balaur never again deployed the Dredgion.

Chronicle of Zumion

When light first graced the land, AION selected an apostle in the name of healing and order.
Her name was Zumion. She was the first of the Daeva, the reaper of suffering, and the mediator of divine will.

Chapter I. Blessing of the Sanctuary

Zumion Temple was Atreia's first sacred sanctum, built with AION's blessing.
The land was in turmoil and awash with blood, and humans were losing hope.
In the midst of all this despair, Zumion followed AION's will and held on tightly to the light, resulting in the erection of a temple.

Centered on the power of healing and purification, the temple functioned as a neutral sanctum for humans and Daeva alike.
The sick were healed, strife was put to rest, and countless priests flocked to follow Zumion's will.

At the center of the priesthood were three figures called Estian, Calliste, and Agathon.

Chapter II. The Rise of Zumion

The temple soon became a site of pilgrimage for believers from all over Atreia.
Zumion was no longer the name of a single figure, but a symbol of a mission of healing, and of a divine order. The healing arts perfected within Zumion Temple spread to all corners of the world,
and the natural restorative arts of purification and Guardite were also developed during this time.

Zumion Temple became a great center of learning, faith, and the art of purification.

Chapter III. Signs of Shadow

This tranquility was short-lived, however, as the Balaur were on the move again after a long period of silence, and the appearance of Dragon Lord Meslamtaeda was a particularly ominous sign.

He rebelled against the very concept of godhood,
seeking to take for himself the powers that AION had bestowed upon humanity and Daeva.

For him, the temples were not mere constructions,
but denials of his very being that must be removed.

Chapter IV. Omen

Many temples lay in ruins, but Zumion Temple stood strong as the last remaining light.

The priests defended their sanctum with great resolve, mobilizing Guardite to ward off the contamination around them. But the encroaching shadows eventually broke even their will.

Chapter V. The Eve of Silence

Meslamtaeda finally stood victorious before Zumion Temple.
The sky was black that day, and the land roared as if vomiting blood.
The temple prepared for the final purification rituals.
All the priests, including Estian, remained within the temple to continue their prayers.

But no one knew that the curse that was about to be unleashed would be more than mere destruction—it would trap the temple and all within in eternal silence.

Concerning Drana Cultivation in Atreia

Author: Principal Researcher Lisansa

Drana is an excellent resource with no end of uses, from food, to power, to weaponry.
After much trial and error, Drana cultivation has now been successfully established all across Atreia.
For the sake of sharing results of research into Drana cultivation, I will describe it according to the different life stages of Drana.

Sowing Stage
Drana seeds in crystal-like form are planted in the ground or implanted in living organisms, and grow by absorbing life force, using the soil or living organisms as fertilizer to grow rapidly.
Germinated sprouts require constant nourishment to keep them from withering.

Growing Stage
Drana can take on many different forms depending on the host or environment, but typically grows as a tree. The shape varies, but beneath the bark, the fertilizing organism turns into a soft solid, and the Drana grows like a fruit.
At this stage, the Drana roots may be cut off and planted to grow more Drana trees.
We have the great Ishtar to thank for this knowledge, which has led to further innovative ways to increase Drana production.

Fruiting Stage

Once the Drana seeds develop inside, the growth is complete. The size of the fruit varies depending on the environment and cultivation methods, and it is said that Tiamat's army once knew how to grow Drana larger than any others.
Regardless, current technological advancements have focused on improving the seeds themselves to increase their raw material content.

When the Drana fruit is ripe, the skin cracks open to allow the Drana inside to be easily harvested.
The skin is removed and only the Drana seeds are left behind following harvesting so that they may grow another Drana fruit.

You came across a boy named Oliver crying at Elim's Rest. He told you he used to live in the nearby village but barely made it out alive when the forest caught fire. His parents had hidden some emergency funds in a secret spot near his home in case something like this happened, but the Blades pushed in before he could do anything. Convinced he was doomed to starve to death, Oliver was extremely grateful for your offer of help, and told you where to find his house and the stash of Kina.

Upon pulling a lever behind the house as instructed, a chest appeared. The emergency funds were found inside, but there was also a letter addressed to someone other than Oliver.

Suspicious, you lied to Oliver and said the chest had been empty. His mood immediately shifted and started rambling before storming off.

You went to find Tao, the young man named in the letter, and handed him the Kina and the letter. Tao recognized the name of Oliver and decided to leave for elsewhere before he showed up.

"If that command document is true... there's still hope to find them."

A Recluse Daeva named Pordhet requested your help at the Abandoned Campsite. After the Blades left the campsite, he was cleaning up after them and happened upon one of their command documents. You read the command document handed over by Pordhet.

The document mentioned relocating some Daeva to Blood Haven—the names of a number of Pordhet's comrades among them. Holding tight to the possibility they might still be alive, Pordhet asked for help in rescuing them.

After many twists and turns, you successfully rescued Pordhet's comrades from Blood Haven. Along the way, you discovered a room Gerod had created, driven by his longing for Nemon. Knowing Nemon had already disposed of him, you agreed to leave it buried in secrecy forever.

"You remember the Black Claw you rescued from the prison?"

Lakiba told you that Chikata has since been causing some trouble, and invited you inside to greet Amunta.

Inside the hideout, Chikata and Amunta were arguing because Chikata wanted to go home to Black Claw Village even though she was not fully recovered. Amunta eventually relented, but asked you to ensure she made it home safely.

An outpost garrisoned by low-level Balaur troops, serving as a watchtower over the Ellun River Midstream and Verteron Fortress Ruins. Any Shugo or Daeva seen passing by will likely be attacked solely for entertainment.
A Balaur Prison Compound located along the Kraka Footpath. Due to its environment being well-suited for incubation of Dratona, it is currently used as a temporary hatching ground.

A graveyard established at a time when countless humans and Daeva were dying daily. The sheer amount of souls laid to rest here, most deprived even of the dignity of being named, has made it a place few wish to step foot near. An increasing number of graverobbers, however, are taking note of rumors of buried treasures.

An underground prison where those defeated in war were locked away. Over the years, the long-forgotten Prison of Oblivion has become filled only with restless dead and swarming rats, but rumors whisper of a lost chronicle hidden deep within its walls.

A temple where Fate Archon candidates once trained and studied Marchutan’s scriptures. Following the massacre of the instructors and candidates by Sigebert’s loyalists, the site is now haunted by vengeful souls who guard the temple's treasures from outsiders.
An outpost garrisoned by the Dratona troops who monitor the Drana Plantation.

An outpost now held by the Flauke Legion. Once protectors of the Purifying Forest, they became deeply demoralized after suffering a brutal defeat to the Balaur. Driven by the power of Fafnite, Commander Flauke is now guilty of innumerous atrocities.

An abandoned cave where a Daeva who betrayed the Blades was imprisoned, tortured, and left to die. It is said the restless spirit of this traitor, together with those of other murdered Daeva, haunts and attacks any who pass through.
A cave that is home to the Giant Karnif Istan—a ferocious beast that emerged as the apex predator in a bitter, cold land without Mau. Strangely enough, it shares a nest with a Debry.
Ruins of the Ancient City of Ru
An outpost of a chasing unit of Balaur, led by Sehna. It is tasked with killing experiments that escape from the stronghold or run amok.

A temple so ancient that its origins are lost to time. Gradually flooded by seawater over eons, most of the structure and the valuables within now lie buried underwater. However, whispers persist of treasure waiting in areas yet to be swallowed by the sea.

A cave that now stands as a tomb to pilgrims who succumbed to Sura mutation. Their fellow Illusion God pilgrims continue to pray inside, wishing them peaceful slumber, but the Sura—whose grudges run deep—may awaken again at any moment.
A hatchery and training ground for Dratona, a new kind of Balaur born in Atreia. Inherently fragile, they are often treated as expendable.
A cave once filled with clean groundwater, now tainted by the contaminated Mystic Spring. With the fresh water cut off, all it attracts is creatures who thrive on its filth.
The Aullaeu worshipped Dragon Lord Tiamat for generations. Even following her fall and the ascendance of Dragon Lord Ishtar, they did not falter in their worship and continue to build altars to her.
A Balaur storage that holds Drana, Drana by-products, and the supplies needed to grow Drana.

The Ancient City of Ru, passed down through legend, is said to have once boasted a highly advanced civilization.
Confirming what lies within has become the life's goal of countless explorers.
A site assumed to be a former part of Zumion Temple. Now little more than broken ruins, perhaps it might contain records of ancient times.
This storage room is where the Balaur imprison Daeva to extract Fafnite from them. It is said that such storage rooms contain not only the Fafnium, but also the Balaur manual on Fafnite and Fafnium.

A former camp for lumberjacks and hunters from the days when the Patamor Plains were still a forest. Long abandoned, it was rumored to have been resettled by outsiders. Now, only their ghosts roam the site, alongside fearless outlaws who have turned the haunted camp into their base of operations.
There are Daeva who, despite not being Sura, have strayed from the Daeva path and sworn to serve the Balaur. This cave is the home to such Daeva Renegades.
A secret library built in Tolbas Forest by the librarian Hypatia to preserve the knowledge of the Elyos.

Karas fled the village to this cave, but their fate could not be avoided. Though sealed in the past, the ravages of time have once again reopened this Karas-infested den. They continue to lurk within, mad and hungry for prey.
A cave used by those seeking the Balaur power over honor of the Mau. Followers of Shaman Kumbahum are growing in strength here.

One of the many hidden Lepharist research centers spread across Eltnen.
The facility is home to a myriad of research initiatives—including processing Drana into energy and breeding test subjects.
However, its test subject research has been halted for reasons unknown.
An outpost garrisoned by Balaur of the Lagta Brigade. Responsible for hunting down any local resistance, they are notorious for being among the most brutal of the Balaur.

The base of the Ratcatchers, a group that kidnaps refugees in Lacephin Village and trades them for profit. Named after their tendency to refer to victims as 'rats', its members infamously revel in the criminality of their actions.
A brutal training ground where Mumu Laborers strive to become warriors. Those who break under the overseer's strict training are cast into the prison's grip.
The place where the soul-shattered cadets of Destruction Archons, slain for defying Hystan's command, are imprisoned in eternal despair

It is not uncommon for those undergoing Sura mutation to deny reality and seek to return to their original forms by curing their symptoms, hiding away as they conduct research through often unethical methods.
A cave where Daeva fleeing the Balaur hid while gathering their strength for a counterattack.

A place where the Fafnium used throughout the Sanctum Outpost is managed by the Lagta Brigade. The Lagta Brigade has been using Fafnium created by Dragon Lord Fafnir to steal the souls of countless Daeva and control their empty flesh. This place is being guarded by Sentinel Nuraka of the Lagta Brigade.

Long ago, treasure hunters fled to an abandoned ruin to escape a Balaur assault. They perished after being trapped within, and lingered on as vengeful revenants. Driven mad, they came to regard the ancient tome within as a priceless treasure, and now serve as its guardians.
A storage housing the Blades' Odylium marauders. Fortified with powerful security devices, it holds vital documents tied to Odylium.

An artificial cave created by Fire Temple worshipers. Much care went into maintaining the cave, as the Guardian statues were relocated in an attempt to counteract Water Aura from the ocean. Now, however, it lies abandoned.
A cave full of Dratona eggs. The adult Dratona Baratuna vigilantly guards the eggs.
A den imprisoning Razekin, a Shulak who survived Fafnite dust poisoning but lost his mind entirely.

As Eltnen suffered relentless invasions by the Balaur and the Lepharists, many Daeva became part of the ever-growing list of casualties. Tifus, a Life Daeva, secretly moved the bodies of the fallen to a secluded cavern in the hopes that his kin could return to AION's embrace.
However, AION's fall made it impossible for the dead to return to Odyle. Instead, they rotted within the cave, mutating into vile contaminations.
Tifus, who sought only to grant his fellow Daeva their final rest, succumbed to the contamination as well.
Burdened by resentment and unable to return to Odyle, he remains forever entombed within the dark cavern as a revenant.
The thieves led by Ugaros. Their main targets are refugees trying to get to the Dawn Legion Base. They are notorious for raiding campsites with refugees on several occasions.

A hideout of wanted criminals who originally worked for the Steel Hammer Merchants until they were caught smuggling goods. Now settled in the eastern Gribade Highland, they continue to target passing merchants.

A Balaur base set up to monitor the area around Black Claw Village. Watch Captain Amurahta keeps a close eye to ensure the local Mau do their work efficiently, and extorts them for their supplies under the pretext of offering them protection.
A cave where a group of Klaw live. It is said that there is a special herb that grows in the Klaw habitat.

A mysterious rift said to lead to the Ancient City of Ru, known only to seasoned explorers.

Rumors claim that the lost records of Ru lie hidden deep within this cave.
Ruins of the Ancient City of Ru

A band of thieves settled in the Pilgrim's Ridge. Their main targets are the residents of Zumion Village and pilgrims traveling to and from there. In addition to robbing pilgrims of their goods, they are also known to enjoy kidnap and blackmail.
Formerly a Legion outpost overseeing the Muspel Volcano Zone, it fell into ruin following a volcanic eruption. It now serves as the base of a cult that worships the volcano.
A marauder hideout hidden within the Purifying Forest. This group particularly despises the Karas and loots all forest inhabitants, Nornirs and Karas alike.

Following the molten lava that flows deep within the cave leads directly into the heart of the Fire Temple. The spirits here, bound to the structure's power, became twisted and corrupted the very day Kromede abandoned the temple.

The battle at the Nahid Brigade Fortress ended in total defeat for the Daeva. Many were captured or succumbed to extinction, and what few survived went into hiding in places such as the Cave of the Defeated.

An outpost occupied by the Balaur. This place was a fierce battlefield between the Balaur and the Daeva, but after the Daeva were defeated, the Balaur took over here. It is now used by the Balaur as an observation post to monitor the Ellun River Marsh.
The miasma grows stronger day by day in a cave full of poisonous plants. Inside, the amount of agrints and slimes contaminated by the plants is steadily rising.

The Creion of Eltnen used their advanced technology to combat the desertification of the region and repel the invading Balaur. However, as Eltnen was never historically a stronghold for their race, their individual efforts quickly hit a wall, forcing most Creion to abandon the wasteland. Yet, a researcher named Malgerre refused to leave, determined to perfect a way to save Eltnen. Continuing his work alone in a small cave, Malgerre’s obsession eventually drove him to use his own body as a test subject. Tragically, the experiment ended in catastrophic failure, mutating him into a hideous monster.

An outpost manned by Balaur of the Lagta Brigade, built to support their research into destroying the Blood Barrier. Whether human or Shulak, any who dare approach Impetusium Square without permission are attacked indiscriminately.
An altar where Naga Wasti performs rites to strengthen the Dragon Lord's power. Wasti is a mighty warrior, feared as the Daeva slayer.
After being defeated by Ishtar's armies, some Daeva suffered extinction, some became Sura, and some even became Apparitions. The wrathful screams of those Daeva Apparitions are heard day and night.

Once a small legion that resisted the Balaur, after a particularly brutal defeat, they decided instead to use illusion magic known as the Eye of Enchantment to abduct villagers in pursuit of expanding their influence.

Inherently inquisitive, the Creion are famed for seeking out dangerous places to conduct dangerous experiments. This cave is one of many such places, abandoned following an experiment that ended in failure. However, perhaps they left some valuable items behind.
A place where an ancient Zumion Priest sealed himself away together with Meslamtaeda's poison, enduring intense agony as he continues his solitary battle.
One of the Lagta Brigade's Fafnite Storages, overseen by the Supervisor Sinah.
A sanctum where the Destruction Archon, sworn to Zikel, find rest. Known as the Warriors' Rest, this ancient site is rumored to hold relics tied to Zikel.
Home to the Hernon Thieves, an offshoot of the Hilsrother Marauders. This group of ne'er-do-wells are known for their relentless targeting of Tsenka Merchants Shugo.

A hiding place storing items stolen by fugitives from Lacephin Village. The stash contains a variety of items, including a book on magic—which was used by one of the fugitives to seal the storage door.
A library built in Altamia Canyon by the librarian Hypatia. Fearing it would be attacked and the accumulated knowledge within lost, she distributed the books across multiple other libraries.

The Ancient City of Ru, passed down through legend, is said to have once boasted a highly advanced civilization.
Confirming what lies within has become the life's goal of countless explorers.
A cave where a rift to the unstable Abyss has appeared. It contains information about the secrets of the Ancient City of Ru.

After the destruction of the Abyss Gate of Verteron Fortress, some of the Klaw that lived in the Abyss have settled in the Verteron Fortress Ruins. The Klaw queen, Karat, spawns from her nest and seeks to expand their territory.

A secret library built by the librarian Musein to preserve the knowledge of the Asmodians, under the sworn protection of the Kerubar. Whispers tell of ancient tomes containing information on the Bulwark.
A hidden cave rich in rare minerals. Crystalline monsters are swarming within.
A twisted pit believed to descend into the Ancient City of Ru, known only to the most daring explorers. Rumors persist that the lost records of Ru are hidden within its depths.
A training base for Fate Archons under Sigebert's command. What looks like an unassuming cave from the outside actually houses an elaborate fortress full of security devices meant to deter intruders.
A pack that hunts indiscriminately in the Tolbas Forest. They don't hesitate to attack other humans or Shugo. In particular, they are catching a lot of Biruta, upsetting the balance of the forest.
Revelations of Khalil foretells the Daeva' fate. A fragment of this prophecy is said to be hidden within this Rock Cave, now held by the Kalgolem.

A cave rumored to be haunted by the souls of Elyos unable to return to Elysea. Stories say that the Elyos here were trapped in Asmodae while investigating the Abyss alongside Deltras, the Guardian of Elysium.

An outpost of elite Balaur forces monitoring and patrolling Dranactus. They oversee Drana cultivation while keeping watch over the area. A teleportation device allows them to rapidly reinforce their forces, making this a key base.

The body of High Priest Hystan, whose soul and mind were stolen by Fafnite, roamed Altgard and slaughtered countless people. When Hystan's body arrived in Moslan Forest, the Nornir gathered the Daeva and sealed the High Priest's body. They left a stele in memory of his victims, containing the truth about High Priest Hystan, and make offerings there.
A base belonging to the notorious criminal Kius and his followers. The bounty on his head from the Notos Legion has grown higher and higher, but no one has dared attempt to capture him.
The Mutated Varg Test Subjects were once human, but no longer remembers who they were. Guarding the treasure as commanded is all they know.
Rumors whisper of treasure hidden in this abandoned Odylium mine, but all who have ventured inside fell victim to swarms of Odyle Spiders.

An underground outpost for Lepharist experiments.
However, things changed once the Krao Vein was discovered below.
The Balaur have largely abandoned the outpost after reporting the phenomenon, leaving only basic defenses and security measures for tracking experiment progress.

A Daeva hiding from the Balaur once cast a spell on the Manduri here for protection. However, the flawed spell caused the Manduri to become exceedingly aggressive. The Daeva fled, leaving only these furious creatures behind.
A den of grave robber Daeva obsessed with an relic buried in a tomb. They've set up camp near the cemetery and are causing havoc. They are notorious even among fellow grave robbers.
The resting place of Kraka, a legendary chieftain of the Tursin Krall. The Krall worship him still—building altars and offering tribute.
A place to store the Aullaeu's belongings. Pinos, Aullaeu's minions, serve as laborers.
A hideout for Daeva who betrayed the Notos Legion. Instead of fighting the Balaur, they now ambush and rob pilgrims on the road. The looted supplies are piled throughout the hideout.

A secret library built by the librarian Hypatia to preserve the knowledge of the Elyos, under the sworn protection of the Kerubar. Whispers tell of ancient tomes containing information on the Bulwark.

A labor training facility where Sapiens under Balaur command are trained to be laborers. Kobolds, Dracuni, and Balaur live together in this space.
Caretaker Sinandash is assigned as the captain of the training facility.
The Cantas Valley is home to a colony of giant mushrooms that grow higher than the trees. These giant mushrooms greatly favor caves with moist soil and adequate humidity.

The lunatic researcher Sellutey intends to create a new world order by combining Lepharist technology with sorcery.
However, his rogue methods made him unpopular among his fellow Lepharists. Eventually, he came to occupy these ancient ruins, where he continues to focus on his life's work.

A research facility where countless Gravi are harvested to evolve into Gravarax.
Gravarax are an object of fascination for some Lepharist researchers due to their natural evolutionary processes. By studying Gravarax, these researchers seek to replicate the same mechanisms of evolution in their own test subjects.

An exile colony home to legionnaires and Cavaliers who committed heinous crimes. Following the Balaur occupation of Verteron, it fell under Aullaeu control and now imprisons those banished from the Urugugu tribe.

An outpost established by Blades in Moslan Forest to facilitate hunting down any surviving Nornir. Rumor has it that somewhere within the outpost lies a treasure chest filled with valuables looted from the Nornir.
A hiding place of Daeva who have strayed from the Daeva path and now serve the Balaur.
A hideout where the surviving true Fate Archons once stayed. Pledging their eternal loyalty to their Empyrean Lord and High Priest, these Archons met their end here, unable to escape.
A secret armory of the Guardians who resisted the Balaur to the last. No one knows if there are still any useful weapons.

The hiding place of Dehinon, who is both Daeva and non-Daeva. Kidnapped and taken to the Nahid Brigade's base, he managed to escape in the process of being turned into a Sura. Hiding in this cave with his comrades, he is slowly losing his sanity.

This is one of the few places with Odylium on Verteron, though the Odylium may have been exhausted. The Sura who escaped from the laboratories of the Nahid Brigade have gathered here, drawn by the Odyle. Some of the Sura were once Guardians, Daeva soldiers of the Elysea. Traces of their honorable Daeva past can be found in their possessions.
This cave is where defeated Guardians hid from the Balaur and eventually met their ends. It holds the records of the Guardians of Verteron, who fought a fierce battle against the Ishtar Brigade.

A cave serving as the hiding place of Deios, a corrupted Spiritmaster who was one of many who lost their way following Kaisinel's extinction and the dissolution of the Illusion Cavaliers. Out of sight of other Daeva, Deios has been researching dangerous magic in hopes of finding a way to control the spirits of Etheria.
A den of the Akilo Thieves who have become somewhat notorious in the Ellun River Midstream.

A recently excavated cave archive that was hidden from the world for a long time.
Likely built to store records detailing the construction of the Eiron Hill ruins nearby, its interior is now too deteriorated to yield any useful data.
Today, all that remains is the wandering spirits of the Life Daeva who once managed the archive.
A cave known to grow rare herbs. However, the animals that ate the herbs grew too strong, and the cave became inaccessible to humans.

Ishtar developed a technology capable of extracting the life force of Daeva and converting it into alternative energy called Surana. Research and development of Surana required the sacrifice of countless Daeva and other lifeforms used as experimental subjects. To facilitate this research, numerous groups of Balaur dedicated themselves to systematically hunting Daeva and other lifeforms, imprisoning them in nearby bases and supplying them to Nahid Brigade Fortress whenever needed.
A cave of violent outcasts that banded together after the Balaur emerged. Lately, their aggression has extended to Daeva, as well as the Balaur.

A small cavern tucked away on the outskirts of the Ruberein Hills. While it appears completely ordinary from the outside, there are whispers of an endless spring of pristine water deep within. Rumor has it that the source of this pure water is an ancient relic left behind by the Life Daeva, hidden far beneath the spring's depths.
Drawn by these tales, bandits from across the region flock to the cave, but the question remains—who will claim this Life relic?

A former hideout and home to the Nornir who protected the forest, until their souls were stolen during an attack by the Blades. Now in ruins, the hideout is filled with the vengeful wraiths driven mad by despair.

A cave deep within the secluded reaches of Cantas Valley, chosen by the Lupyllini to make their nests. Long used by bandits from nearby mountains to hide their looted treasures, the presence of Lupyllini has made it all but impossible for humans to approach, leaving the treasures piled inside to gather dust with nobody to lay claim to them.
A cave containing abnormal amounts of Fungie. Rumor says that treasure lies deep within, but none have successfully ventured far enough inside.
A temporary home for the Draconute scouts who monitor the area around Drana Plantation.
One of the storages used by the Blades when they were mainly operating in Morheim. Gerod is said to have frequented the repository despite the area's steep terrain.

Once an annex attached to the Eltnen Barrier Tower, this area served as a final refuge for the Life Daeva when the tower collapsed.
In the end, the Balaur stormed the halls, slaughtering nearly all the Daeva hidden within.
Yet, even in the shadow of death, life still blooms. It was here that Kion, the very last of the Life Daeva, was able to ascend.

The Blades' former base from when they were still active in Morheim. As remote as it is barren, it was the perfect location for them to continue their activities without alerting the residents of Patamor Village or Kromede's followers.
A jail situated under the Verteron Fortress. Though currently under Krall control, it still contains many relics and writings of Illusion Cavaliers.
A cave where a passage to the unstable Abyss has appeared. It contains information about the Ancient City of Ru.
During the Karas massacres, even the nobles could not escape their fate. Altgard's slaughterers herded the noble families suspected of being Karas into a single ossuary and imprisoned them.

A cave created to shield the Fire Temple from the humid ocean air. For eons, the Spirit guarding it remained faithful to an ancient promise made with Kromede—only to be consumed by wrath after rumors that she abandoned the temple and fled.
The nest of the Mutant Valka, a giant insectoid that was mutated by contaminants leaking out from the crashed Dredgion.

A vault containing the riches of the Barrier Tower Fortress. Concentrated fire from the Balaur has reduced its entrance to rubble, giving it the unassuming appearance of a cave. The valuables within are still intact, though guarded by the wraiths of Daeva who fell during the attack.

A valley where Daeva resisting the Balaur invasion sought refuge, only to have it become their tomb following a Dredgion bombardment. Many who fought here had been serving since even before the Balaur invasion.
The underground part of the fallen Verteron Fortress. It is used by the Krall as their residence.
Moslan Forest bandits have made a hideout out of an old prison for Asmodian Daeva.
A site of pilgrimage where worshippers of Kaisinel stop and write devotionals. Popularized by a legend that he once stayed here briefly, it is now home only to lost spirits.
The place where Spatalos, former high commander of the Verteron Legion, sealed away Vamana, a vanguard captain of the Drakan. According to folklore, the echoes of their battle can still be heard.

A cave occupied by Naga who reluctantly follow Sigebert's command in the absence of their leader, Dragon Lord Fafnir. They share frosty relations with the Fate Archons, and consider the Krall to be beneath them.
A breeding ground for raising Tayga, the beasts wielded by the Black Claw Mau. The breeding ground is always full bloodshed and howling from these beasts.
The main base of a Taytra Brigade Kurpak unit under Sigebert's command. The unit is made up of swift and decisive soldiers that can be deployed anywhere in Iralcig Highland and Muspel Volcano Zone.
A Draconute battalion is being temporarily stationed here to keep an eye on the Calderon Canyon.
The ruins of a destroyed sanctum, said to contain records written by Empyrean Lord Zikel.

Most of the Varg who escaped from the Lepharist Research Center became minions of the Dragon Lords, but some of them scattered and formed their own packs. The Varg who have settled in caves near the Purifying Forest slaughter or capture rare animals in the forest for illegal trade.

A spring that was abandoned following the Balaur Invasion. Treasures moved here during its construction still remain. However, the area is highly dangerous, as Slimes contaminated by the Mystic Spring of Anathe roam the area.
A secret library built in Basfelt by Musein, a librarian who sought to preserve the knowledge of the Asmodians. Whispers tell of ancient tomes containing information on the Bulwark.

The forward base of Dignuaka, the 62nd Unit Commander of the Ishtar Taruna Brigade.
 During a routine patrol, Digunaka was impressed by the highly efficient Drana energy the Lepharists created, and has been using the energy to evolve and surpass his own limits.
Those who hold twisted beliefs about Zikel gather in this repentance room. This group of fanatics, claiming to be devout followers of Zikel, have only deepened the misunderstandings surrounding him.
A cave where a passage to the Abyss has appeared. It contains information about the Ancient City of Ru.

When the Ishtar Brigade laid waste to Eltnen, the Life Daeva paid a heavy toll in blood. Those who survived withdrew to hidden outposts, quietly working to restore their ruined home.
But as the Lepharists invaded, the last of the Life Daeva were forced into hiding and ultimately disappeared.
Though this cave once sheltered them, it now stands empty and forgotten, stripped of its original purpose.
A prayer hall within the Aullaeu Village, where a fanatical band of Aullaeu devoted to Ishtar is said to gather.
The cliffs of the Cantas Valley feature natural caves of various shapes and sizes, favored as hideouts by the many poachers who ply their illicit trade in and around the valley.

A cave inhabited by the Biruta, a unique creature found in Tolbas Forest and prized by the Shugo for the special properties of their leaves. The gentle-natured Biruta live quietly in small family groups throughout the cave.
The main base of a bandit group occupying Calderon Canyon. They expanded their power using illegal explosives and now pillage anyone in sight, human or Shugo alike.
The Drana Depository of the Balaur, guarded by the Depository Manager Arya, infamous for his brutal slaying of Daeva.

The ruins of a temple on a sky island, brought down by a direct strike from a Balaur Dredgion. It has since become the lair of renegade Daeva, who extort and murder any other Daeva who cross their path.
An altar in a cave made by a Fire Temple worshiper. Though it once held ancient tomes revering the Fire Temple, it has been abandoned after an Artifact Fragment fell.

A Balaur surveillance base built to aid the search for the Ascension Artifact. Functionally a forward base, it collects intel from the fake Fate Archons and reports any findings to the Fafnir Brigade's main forces. The base is littered with Fafnium, which is used to trap the souls of Daeva captured by the fake Fate Archons. Much of the victims tend to be Kromede's followers.

Most Eiron Hill refugees are peaceful and law-abiding, maintaining good relations with the Tsenka Merchants and Chloris.
Drok and his band of outlaws are an outlier. By inciting disgruntled refugees to desert their camp, Drok has established a base for him and his group. Now operating as marauders, they survive on scraps of the chaos left behind by the Hilsrother Marauders and Lepharists.
A pirates' treasure storage hidden beneath Idun's Lake. After being discovered and claimed by the Blades, it has been managed by Custodian Chakkerman.
Within this cave, Zikel's zealots recklessly offer sacrifices in twisted faith. The gathered offerings of victims are presented as tribute to Zikel.

A floating island that broke away during the collapse of the Arkanis Sky Temple, now serving as a Balaur sky outpost. It is overseen by Dinakra, a Balaur who is content with his rank of outpost commander and has little interest in pursuing greater power.

A place where the Nornir Priestess Soirel would revere the memory of the dead alongside believers, until a sudden attack by the Balaur resulted in all those present having their souls taken from them. Now the memorial stands unmaintained and unvisited.

A hideout Verdandi stayed in when she came to Morheim with Skuld—before she settled in Patamor Village. Now, the area is occupied by Indnath's forces, who have been chasing Nemon all the way from Altgard.

A library created in Moslan Forest by Musein, a librarian who sought to preserve the knowledge of the Asmodians by creating a secret library. Whispers tell of ancient tomes on the Bulwark kept within this library's depths.

A temporary base for Kromede, back when she was still active in Morheim. Abandoned ever since Kromede claimed the Sky Island as her base, it is now occupied by servants of Fafnir bewitched by the Domination Stone.

The hideout of Selmar and his fellow Daeva, who are driven by delusions to mercilessly attack innocent Daeva. They believe themselves to be the only true Daeva, and all Daeva who pass through to be their enemies.

A group of thieves based in Western Gribade Highland. Originally, they preyed on nearby refugees, but now they cooperate with the Blades, handing over to them any suspicious outsiders passing through.

Following Kaisinel's disappearance, contracts with the spirits were broken and Etheria grew increasingly unstable, resulting in many spirits turning violent. This cave is one such place overrun with unruly spirits.
A rest stop for Kuru working under the Aullaeu, where they can often be seen lounging around after a hard day's work.

Krall are assigned by the Balaur to handle the disposal of the large amounts of waste produced by experiments conducted in Nahid Brigade Fortress, and of the byproducts produced by the nearby Drana Plantation. The number of Krall specialized in these tasks is substantial enough to require an entire barracks.

A band of bandits settled at the bottom of the Canyon. They appeared here after the illusionary enchantment that protected Zumion Village and the Canyon was removed. They cause trouble by stealing and raiding the nearby Notos Legion bases. They also attack the Spirits traveling to and from the bottom of the Canyon, causing the Spirits to become violent.
A ancient armory of the Destruction Archons, dutifully guarded by Archons through the ages. Rumor says they protect a secret treasure deep within.
An ancient cave where the Lepharist once conducted Krao experiments. Now abandoned, but the test subjects are said to still wander around the cave.

Spirit Flowers have been known to grow in some hidden caves along the middle reaches of the Ellun River. Once common, they have become increasingly rare due to pollution and indiscriminate illegal harvesting for use as a medicinal herb or ingredients for magic. A number of groups have occupied the caves and are indiscriminately harvesting Spirit Flowers illegally.

Sura are Daeva who mutated after having all of their life energy drained by the Balaur. A number of Sura secluded themselves in caves while they still retained their sanity, attempting to halt their mutation. Ultimately, however, all succumbed to their fate of becoming mindless monsters.
An outpost of the Balaur scouts patrolling the Altamia Canyon area. A number of innocent residents of Altamia Canyon are imprisoned inside in terrible conditions.
A den of criminals exiled from Safe Haven, led by Korhe, who tore the village apart with his trickery. It is rumored to be filled with valuables and other loot stolen from the village.

A supply base that once stored and distributed combat provisions for the Ishtar Brigade during the Balaur's ancient war. It was particularly notorious for its mobile bombs, which inflicted massive Daeva casualties. Even now, long after the Balaur have occupied Eltnen, several of these mobile bombs remain deep within the base. Due to the passage of time, no one dares to salvage them out of fear that they may detonate unpredictably. Only the Balaur send occasional patrols to inspect the bombs and monitor the state of the base.

An outpost established by the Balaur outside the Sanctum Outpost. Though disguised as a simple outpost, it is actually a facility for testing Draconute modification, with many violent Draconutes who have slipped beyond Drakan control.
This ruin holds ancient Daeva chronicles, but now exiled Mau who broke their oaths have claimed it as their own.
A underwater cave lair of Daine of Tears, the Water Spirit, who escaped from the cave where the Etheria Rift formed. The spirit without the pact-bearer is now in a highly unstable state.

A cave where pilgrims worshipping the Illusion God practiced meditation. The High Priestess of Illusion summoned Spirits to guard this place for the pilgrims, but after strange things began happening in the garden following her disappearance, pilgrims gradually stopped coming.
Now, only the Spirits remain, guarding an empty cave.

In their darkest hour, a number of Daeva gathered all they had and fled to a hidden cave behind the Basfelt Waterfall. Some ventured out to scout but never returned. Overcome by fear, those left behind stayed in this final refuge, waiting and slowly fading away.
A temporary base for Indnath, who has been chasing Nemon ever since the Lagta Fortress in Altgard. The base is meant to accommodate his forces temporarily until they can eliminate Nemon.

A small rest stop that was originally home to the loggers of Moslan Forest before being taken over by a band of thieves after the forest burned down. The thieves hunt forest creatures or rob refugees who pass through.

A site that once housed records of research conducted by a Balaur named Iagosh and some humans. Today, all of those records have been destroyed or relocated, and the facility now serves as a temporary storage for all tribute collected from the Shugo.
A hidden refuge where the Reckless Jonas, who fled the Blades fearing punishment, hides with his followers. It was once a sanctuary for ascetics' training.

This cave is rumored to contain a miraculous cure-all mushroom.
But none who've entered in search of it have ever returned.
Home to an Agrint contaminated by Drana. A valuable treasure is said to lie unattended somewhere inside.

A site where a small legion resisting the Balaur was annihilated. Daeva soldiers whose bodies and souls have been split now wander aimlessly. The Balaur intend to seal these specters within the ruins and repurpose them into an immortal brigade.

A cavern occupied by the outlaws of the Patamor Plains. Composed primarily of former Blades members, this gang has risen to infamy by robbing travelers and merchants journeying between Altgard and Morheim.
The entrance to a subterranean cave system flooded with groundwater. Rumors speak of treasure awaiting in the depths of the cave, drawing the attention of fortune seekers time and time again.

The Three Sisters of Fate who lead the Nornir are brilliant diviners and prophets. Some of their students once claimed to be greater prophets than their teachers, only to meet their end in this cave after they hid away in fear of a future where they saw themselves turning into Karas.

A base for legionnaire outlaws. They attempted to raid Zumion Village, but were repelled by the Notos Legion and ended up settling here. They make a living looting supplies traveling to and from the highland and raid Notos Legion bases.

A cave located in the Contaminated Marsh, polluted by the sewage and refuse of Nahid Brigade Fortress and the Drana Plantation. Among the waste are a number of documents detailing the Balaur's Surana experiments.

A facility where the Balaur imprison experimental subjects for post-experiment monitoring. Those who underwent mutation and those still retaining human form are confined together, creating a tense atmosphere.

This is a gathering place for the Daeva deserters from the Illusion Cavaliers. When the Illusion Cavaliers were exterminated, many Daeva despaired, abandoned their pride as Daeva, and left the fortress. They have gone their own way to live harsh, brutal lives.
Zikel's zealots grow their power within these underground caves. Corrupted followers blindly worship the kept records of Zikel, spreading false faith throughout Altgard.
A cave claimed as a base by a Draconute warband led by Lamnah, the ruthless Scouts Captain of the Lagta Brigade.

Even noble blood could not save you from the plague that began to spread after Odyle became depleted. Behit, the last remaining heir of a noble family that stayed outside the Bulwark, buried his family with his own hands after they became Karas, and then entered the Abandoned Grave and locked himself within.
A cave used by Aullaeu Shamans for their ritual studies, guarded by Konutins stationed in the area.

Some of the Shulak criminals who roamed the Abyss continued their criminal activities even after settling in Altgard. In particular, a smuggler named Sumakhi will stop at nothing to make a profit and is now notorious among Daeva and humans for his brutality.

A Karas den located in northern Morheim. Originally a hideout for a small group of Nornir, it was eventually raided by the Balaur. Most of its inhabitants were either murdered for resisting or processed as materials for Fafnite, leaving behind a cursed legacy that deters anyone from approaching the area.

A base for members of the Nahid Brigade patrolling the Kraka Footpath, with a particular focus on the direction of Zumion Village. It also serves as a hub for gathering small amounts of Drana generated in the outskirts and transporting it in bulk to the Nahid Brigade's main force.
Producing Fafnite always requires live human or Daeva. For this, Drakan Homish built the prison compound for imprisoning both human and Daeva.

A plantation for Drana built by the Balaur. These plantations can be found all across Elysea, as Drana are able to develop unique characteristics depending on their environment. The vegetation in this specific area is known to cause mutations in Drana.
A cave located deep in the Tolbas Forest. The cave is inhabited by highly poisonous plants and animals, making it difficult to access.
It is the grave of an unknown reader who never let go of a book until the moment of the death. There may have been some rare books in the reader's collection.
A granary used by the residents of Verteron until Dratona forces turned it into a Balaur lair. The Dratona captain, Nagto, has wasted no time in pocketing the accumulated grain.
A burial vault beneath Verteron Fortress. It likely contains a great number of Daeva relics, with its underground location having allowed it to escape Balaur bombardment.

A research facility packed with the Lepharists' most fanatical and aggressive special operations units. Driven by an obsession with strength, these radicals willingly become test subjects for their own experiments, fostering an atmosphere of ruthless competition in the name of enhancing combat performance.

A deep gorge formed by tectonic shifts.
Suspicious individuals of unknown identity have regularly been seen coming and going.

A fortress occupied by outlaws operating in the Lankusis Plateau and led by their captain, Rumer.
In a time where fully ascended Daevas are scarce, Rumer’s gang is a rare exception; every single member is a Daeva with wings.
Utilizing this advantage, they have built a stronghold on a sky island far beyond the reach of most people, giving them free rein to terrorize the region.
A cave where a passage to the unstable Abyss has appeared. It contains additional information about the ancient city of Ru.
The Scribe's Room is believed that it was part of the Zumion Temple. The scribe left behind many records, but those on paper have been weathered away by time, and only a few stone tablets remain.
A cave used for mass burial of those killed by Meslamtaeda's poison. After consuming the contaminated corpses, the Targos inside have mutated and taken over the cave for themselves.
Once the stronghold of a legion known as the Golden Branch Brigade. Now, it is occupied by a group of thieves stealing hard-earned Odyle found by refugees at the destroyed Eltnen Barrier Tower.

A spring near Muspel Volcano, located under a cliff so dangerous that not even the treasure hunter Kromede has dared to get close—or at least, according to the rumors. Many a starry-eyed explorer has ventured here in hopes of surpassing Kromede's glory.
The ground beneath Altgard is weakening due to underground tunnels used by the burrowing insectoid. It is said the burrowing insectoids dwell in this cave.
The thieves trading in suspicious herbs. There is a foul smell in the area. Frequently visited by those looking for suspicious herbs. The thieves loot nearby farms to fund their needs.
