The major difference between humans and Daeva is the "immortality" of the latter. A Daeva's appearance is permanently fixed to that at the moment of their Ascension, but upon the destruction of a Daeva's physical body, rather than dying, their soul returns to the Odyle flow while a new body is reconstructed, at which point they return to life.
At this moment, the separated soul can immediately find its body and resurrect through a "Kibelisk" to which the soul is bound.
However, were a Daeva to die in a place devoid of Odyle,  or suffer an attack so powerful that the soul and body cannot be reunited, their soul will succumb to "extinction."
Nevertheless, this practical immortality means the concept of an irreversible "death" remains hard to grasp for many Daeva.

A Krall brainwashed to follow the Balaur.
It has a ferocity that is uncontrollable even with the Balaur's modifications.

Heladrir loved Giselle. Even though Giselle had a lover, his love did not fade. When Giselle was unfairly dragged into the underground grave, her lover gave up on her, but Heladrir did not give up. Heladrir secretly infiltrated the underground grave to save Giselle. However, Heladrir could not find Giselle and could not even confirm whether she was alive. While wandering through the cave below the underground grave, he was captured by enraged Karas. The Karas tied Heladrir to the wall and left him there. After a long time, Heladrir also became a Karas and forgot his Daeva memories, but he never forgot Giselle.

After the skies of Atreia were torn asunder, the Empyrean Lords of Elysea and Asmodae became similarly divided.
Yet their power is fundamentally one.

As a being destined to become "Arch Daeva" and carry on AION's will, you must experience the memories of the Empyrean Lords and understand the complete form of AION's power.
Through this process, you will ascend to become the absolute being destined to save Atreia.

Due to the <QK>Last War</>, the Tower of Eternity, AION, collapsed, and its fragments scattered throughout Atreia. Although AION was shattered, fragments of its consciousness remained in the dream. Asahr is the entity that manages AION's unending dream, and one of AION's fragments, representing AION's Willpower. Asahr watches over the Daeva who possess AION's fragments in the dreams and guides their path.

A creature living in the better part of Ellun River.
It appeared for the first time after the Last War. Hostile to Daeva.

The closest confidant to Kaisinel, the High Priestess of the Illusion Cavaliers. She is the strongest Spiritmaster in Elysea and the most knowledgeable about magic. Reda had the opportunity to take refuge inside the Bulwark, but she remained outside. This was not only to fulfill her duty as High Priestess to protect the Core but also because she believed the Daeva behind the Bulwark would return to aid those outside. Reda fulfilled her duty while protecting her daughter Teina, who remained outside the Bulwark with her. However, the harsh environment outside the Bulwark gradually broke the High Priestess's heart.

Kromede is in a state of being dominated by the Mirror of Desire. The Mirror of Desire, one of the ancient Daeva's treasures sealed in the Fire Temple, had been watching Kromede for a long time, waiting for the day it would consume Kromede. When Kromede, cornered, weakened as her body and mind collapsed, it seized the opportunity and consumed her. The Mirror of Desire extracts only Kromede's intense desires and controls the Fire Temple in Kromede's form.
An elderly Aullaeu shaman praying to Ishtar. Though not a chieftain, he is feared and respected by the Aullaeu.

A sacred bird of the Urugugu tribe. Auldor is originally a legendary bird appearing in Aullaeu's traditions. The Aullaeu had long wanted to summon the sacred bird they considered to embody the Core of the Aullaeu, but it was impossible. However, after serving Ishtar, the Aullaeu, who received some of the power of Ishtar, were able to summon Auldor. The sacred bird of the Urugugu tribe soars through the skies of Urugugu Canyon, protecting the Aullaeu.

An illusion that warns those who approach the Coastal Cave. Summoned by Reda, the High Priestess of Illusion, it resembles her in appearance. Reda sealed the Coastal Cave with a Barrierstone and placed the Illusion there not only to protect intruders from the Sura within, but also, it seems, to protect the Sura inside. The exact reason remains unknown.

Tyrkes, once a member of the Legion Outlaws, wandered throughout Verteron before settling in the Altamia Highlands. He tried to occupy Zumion Village with his outlaw Daeva, but his attempt was thwarted by the Notos Legion, forcing him to settle outside the village. Tyrkes has not given up and continues to bide his time, waiting for an opportunity to strike against the Notos Legionnaires and Zumion Village.

A special Guardite among the summoned pets used by ancient Daeva.
Summoned by Estian, the name signifies an unwavering love for Zumion. After the seal was corrupted, it transformed into a monster.

A Sura who manages the Disposal Plant at Nahid Fortress. Modified for combat specialization, it has strong combat capabilities but retains no memories, personality, or even form remaining from its time as a Daeva. It was used as a soldier to protect Ishtar Castle, but after the Dawn Legion attack on Poeta, it was demoted to the Disposal Plant. It finds Daeva who try to steal things to be extremely annoying.

A Drakan from Meslamtaeda's special forces, the Seker Strike Forces. He operates independently to spy on and disrupt Daeva.  He has the ability to create territories within with he can move unseen using the powers granted by Meslamtaeda. Normal Daeva cannot detect him, but those with a "Daeva Sense" can find his tracks.
A disciplined, patient, and intelligent Drakan. His mission is to spy on the Daeva' main bases. His mission is to scout rather than kill, but when he wants a taste of Daeva' blood, he will deliberately leave his tracks to lure his prey.

A Sura who was sealed in the Coastal Cave of Verteron Cantas Valley. Once a prisoner of the Balaur, it became a Sura and then escaped from the Nahid Fortress laboratory, drifting to the Coastal Cave. It is presumed to have been a powerful Daeva before becoming a Sura, and although completely irrational, it wears a necklace from its Daeva days.

Jenaki the Ruler of Blood 
[Description to be written]

Arch Daeva are shattered Fragments of AION, a great being of the universe, and thus, all Arch Daeva shall return to perfection by collecting the fragments and become complete once more. The Ascension Artifact lets its owner absorb other Arch Daeva to reach AION.

Those who swear the oath and overcome the trial shall rise as Arch Daeva, and ascend higher as they absorb the fate and abyss of other Arch Daeva.

After ascending as Arch Daeva, the heroes enter the Bulwark—a world free from the threats of the Balaur. Inside this realm, five agents govern society as representatives of the extinct gods. Reunited with Phernos, the heroes are assigned to the Elysium Guard, where Caelid serves.

As they carry out their duties as guards, the heroes meet various agents. Most are indifferent about gathering the Cores, but the Agent of Light criticizes them and proposes uniting to change the world. With Caelid, the heroes join the Masked Corps under the Agent of Light's command.

The Masked Corps begins eliminating political rivals and Arch Daeva, prompting Arch Daeva Esh to form a resistance force. The two sides confront each other while seeking Vaizel's Core. After securing Vaizel's Core, the Agent of Light attempts to eliminate the heroes and the Arch Daeva at the same time, with Caelid also betraying the heroes.
The heroes realize that the Agent of Light aims to become a god by completing the Artifact of Light, and they team up with the Arch Daeva to reclaim the stolen Vaizel's Core.

The heroes and the Arch Daeva resolve to stop the Agent of Light together and complete the artifact themselves.

Carlotte was originally a Daeva of the Notos Legion. However, he was overwhelmed by the fear of fighting the Balaur to protect the people of Zumion Village. Kalote fled his duty and the village, taking a precious relic with him. He later created and settled in a hideout in the southern highlands with his followers.

A Templar of the Dawn Legion. Before the Last War, she was a promising Guardian and a talent who was undoubtedly expected to become a Legion High Commander someday. After the collapse of the Guardians, she led the surviving Guardians in resistance activities and is now a member of the Dawn Legion. Even after losing her lover and Dawn Legion Vice High Commander, Perion, in the battle of Nahid Fortress, she did not give in and fulfilled her duty as a Daeva. She respects Caelid but has some doubts about Caelid's plan to go beyond the Bulwark. She followed Caelid's reckless Poeta operation in the hope that she might find the missing Perion.

A Drakan officer from the Lagta Brigade under Fafnir. He is tasked with managing the Fafnium planted in various places in Altgard and collecting Fafnite, aboard a Dredgion. The Collapsed Oracle is one of the places Rathman visits. Although he dislikes Daeva, he tolerates the Blades for their efficiency in capturing humans to turn into Fafnite. He has a strong desire for power and an obsession with success, so he uses Fafnite implanted in his own gear.

Transcending the Physical Form to Achieve True Freedom
Bakarma, who absorbed the energy flowing into the portal with his entire being, brushes through the boundaries of various dimensions alongside the portal.
Having crossed through dimensions and encountered various entities, Bakarma has come to regard the immense axis that spans the world, as well as the beings known as Elyos, Asmodians, and the Balaur, as insignificant.
He seeks to break free from the confines of being categorized as the Balaur.
Shedding his shell-like physical body and breaking the boundaries of soul and spirit, he aims to transcend the limitations of the souls possessed by Elyos, Asmodians, and the Balaur to become a free being.

The conditions for completing oneself and reaching a transcendent stage are as follows:
First, the bloodline of a transcendent being.
Second, overcoming limitations and coming to understand the principles of the universe.

In Bakarma's case, he came to understand the the principles of the universe and achieved transcendence by passing through various dimensions via the portal.
Afflicted Bakarma, not yet entirely free from his physical body, continues to meditate in a levitating state.

A high shaman of the Urugugu tribe. He is called the Judicator, responsible for punishing those who violate rules or religious doctrines. Although his status is lower than the tribal chief, his influence is comparable. He is a figure of fear among the Aullaeu.

A Drakan officer from the Lagta Brigade under the Fafnir, who manages Dranactus Underkeep. With a cruel personality, he finds life in Altgard boring. He tortures or experiments on imprisoned Daeva. Not only Daeva who oppose the Balaur, but also those whom Santras personally finds interesting are imprisoned for fun. Interesting prisoners are also offered as gifts to Fafnir.

The female mate of Tyrant Ursan appearing in the Hero Quest Step.
Having recently lost her young, she comes out of the cave and massacres anything she sees (especially humans). She has become extremely ferocious.

Reda, High Priestess of Kaisinel, remained outside the Bulwark due to her duty to protect the Core of Illusion. To protect the Core of Illusion and her daughter Teina, she did not manage the Illusion Cavaliers and did not participate in the Daeva' resistance war. However, her duty never ended, and the promised reinforcements from within the Bulwark never arrived. When Teina, Reda's last hope, was killed by the Balaur, Reda abandoned her duty as High Priestess. Her mind collapsed, and she poured her anger and sorrow onto Phernos.

A member of the Blades operating in Morheim. One of the long-time members of the Blades, he was also a colleague who worked with Nemon when Nemon was in the Blades. Nua recognized Nemon's achievements, so he was greatly shocked when Nemon left the Blades. Currently, he is more motivated than anyone else to torment and hinder Nemon.

A special artifact within AION's dream. The dreams of all beings in Atreia that have passed through Odyle flow remain within the artifact, and these dreams can be recalled through it. However, since AION collapsed, some of the dreams recorded in the artifact have been altered or scattered.

After Kaisinel and Lumiel disappeared, the Spirit King considered the contract with the Daeva to be over and tried to control all the spirits. Gartua, a minion of the Spirit King, has the power to influence space and can freely move between the gaps of Atreia and Etheria. Following the Spirit King's orders, it either summons spirits from Atreia back to Etheria or brainwashes those still connected to the Daeva, turning them into loyal minions of the Spirit King.
A biological weapon of the Nahid Brigade guarding the Drana Plantation.

Gerod, Nemon's fated adversary and leader of the Blood Blades, used Fafnite to transform and empower himself. Gerod was provided with Fafnite as a reward for siding with the Balaur and offering Daeva. Fafnite is generally unusable by Daeva, but Gerod found a way to transform his body by directly implanting it. Once transformed, he can never return to his Daeva form, but the Blood Blades does not value Daeva identity. Gerod was willing to give up everything, if only to defeat Nemon.
A creature born from the contaminated mud of the marsh.
One of the managers of the Dranactus barracks area. He is in a position equal to Warden Santras.

Weathered Gadioton Monster Description

An elder Daeva who has witnessed the historical moments of Atreia from the Elyos-Asmodian War to the Balaur War, and finally, the Last War. His original name is Akarios, and he was a member of the Storm Legion. He is a survivor who witnessed Zikel's wrath in Asmodae and returned alive. After enduring the long Elyos-Asmodian War, he lived in seclusion in Poeta for a long time. When the entirety of Atreia was in crisis during the Last War, he ended his seclusion. He is also a close friend of Reda and entrusted Reda to fulfill her duty to protect the Core before going inside the Bulwark. He has now emerged from within the Bulwark, believing that the Elysea needs the Core.

These are fragments of AION's dream. They have fallen all over Atreia, and each fragment is guarded by a protector. Only those who have the potential to become an Arch Daeva can discover, activate them, and read the information contained within the fragments.

Asahr watches over the Daeva who possess AION's fragments in the dreams and guides their path.

An apparition that holds a part of the memory and power of Kaisinel, the God of Illusion and Fear, Spiritmasters, and Clerics. Kaisinel disappeared when he erected the Bulwark in Elysea, but he left a remnant of his apparition in the Ardus Shrine to protect the Core of Illusion. The apparition resembles Kaisinel in lifetime, and his thoughts and speech are similar. However, the thought entity is only a very small part of Kaisinel's existence.

One of the combat-type test subjects created by the Lepharists and offered to the Balaur as a sign of cooperation. Berk fought for the Balaur in the Last War, but was shattered during the intense and prolonged conflict. The broken Berk freed itself from its restraints and went on a rampage, disobeying the orders of both the Lepharist and the Balaur. To contain this, the Lepharists retrieved Berk after the war and imprisoned and sealed it in Krao Cave. After the Lepharists left Krao Cave, Berk, left alone, tried to evolve into a stronger being by repeating division and fusion.
A Drakan who whips laborers in the Plantation.
An Aullaeu warrior who manages looted goods and captured Shugo, and guards the frontier.

A dream afterimage that reflects a part of Siel, one of AION's two guardians and the Empyrean Lord who governs time. Siel sacrificed herself during the Great Catastrophe to prevent the collapse of the tower. Even after Siel perished, her memories remained in AION's dream. Siel, who became a dream afterimage, still feels compassion for AION's creations and seeks to guide Atreia on the right path.

A powerful figure in Altgard's Safe Haven, possessing significant Odyle resources. She was also involved in suppressing the soulless Hystan, the disaster of Moslan Forest, alongside the Nornir. She infiltrated Ishalgen's Fafnir Fortress to find the <QK>High Priest's Fafnite</> and ended up rescuing the survivors of the Hugo Mercenaries, who were in danger while also searching for treasure. She has a cold personality, but many follow her, including Ulgorn. Other than seeking the High Priest's Fafnite for revenge, little else is known about her.

A valiant warrior of the Urugugu tribe. He is responsible for the safety of the Aullaeu residents and shamans living in the Urugugu Canyon. He is slightly dissatisfied with the lower status of soldiers compared to shamans but is faithful to his duty to protect the canyon.

Following the "Last War", the AION Tower was shattered completely.
Empyrean Lords and Daeva alike suffered a great weakening of their power as a consequence, and Elysea and Asmodae fell victim to renewed assault by the "Dragon Lords."

Yet through the fragments of shattered AION, new hope was born.
Beings born with these fragments within them began to emerge, possessing the potential to carry on AION's will.
Through communication with "Asahr," the steward of AION's dream, they may experience the memories embedded within the fragments of AION and awaken new power.

A ritualist of the Urugugu tribe, who served Ishtar at the Aullaeu Altar. It was a devoted Aullaeu with excellent healing abilities. It resisted Reda's magic that invaded the Aullaeu Altar but eventually died. Aulisa's dead body was used as a sacrifice for Reda's forbidden Scarlotus magic. Reawakened by forbidden magic, Aulisa was very different from its former self.

A special artifact within AION's dream. The dreams of all beings in Atreia that have passed through Odyle flow remain within the artifact, and these dreams can be recalled through it. However, since AION collapsed, some of the dreams recorded in the artifact have been altered or scattered.

A contracted Spirit of an outstanding superior Spiritmaster belonging to the Illusion Cavaliers.
After the Spiritmaster perished, they could not return to Etheria and are now wandering the canyon.

Ulgorn, a human who failed to become a Daeva, endured a perilous journey with Nemon. Caught up in Nemon's affairs, they faced disaster. In his dying moments, Gerod used Fafnite on him. Ulgorn was strengthened by Fafnite but became a monster that forgot all memories of his comrades. Perhaps Ulgorn had prepared for such a death.
An Odylium Spirit guarding the Eternal Isle.
A wandering Mau shaman who acts independently in the eastern canyon. He was expelled from the Black Claw Village.

The God of Destruction, Gladiators, and Templars. He was cruel and enjoyed battle. He also triggered the Elyos-Asmodian War by destroying the Storm Legion in Morheim. After the Last War, Zikel exhausted most of his power to create the Bulwark in Asmodae. Though weakened, he stood alongside the Destruction Archons to defend Altgard, but ultimately deemed it impossible to stop Fafnir. Zikel sacrificed himself and the Destruction Archons to create a Blood Barrier in Impetusium and perished.

A Pino is a wooden doll created by the Aullaeu by enchanting a piece of wood. Though lifeless, it can move thanks to magic and obeys the Aullaeu's commands faithfully. Most Pinos are weak-bodied and used for simple chores, but Pinopi was specially crafted for combat among them. Currently, its performance is recognized, and it is used as a gatekeeper for the Root Cellar.

A kind-hearted shaman who takes care of the Aullaeu soldiers on the outskirts of Aullaeu Forest.

A special spirit born and raised in Etheria. It came from Etheria to Atreia through a rift created after the contract between Daeva and spirits was broken and settled in a tree in Verteron. It holds the pure power of Etheria and uses that power to keep Spirit's Rest from being contaminated. Although it considers Spirit's Rest its home, it was sucked into the Etheria Rift by the Spirit King's orders a while ago.

A sacred animal of Cantas Valley.

Personal Guard Irima

A Drakan from Meslamtaeda's special forces, the Seker Strike Forces. He operates independently to spy on and disrupt Daeva.  He has the ability to create territories within with he can move unseen using the powers granted by Meslamtaeda. Normal Daeva cannot detect him, but those with a "Daeva Sense" can find his tracks.
Zrash is cruel and likes to slaughter. He is self-centered and undisciplined. He was transferred from the Strike Forces after causing trouble. He is generally happy with his current job of working alone and hunting the Daeva, but is sometimes unhappy at not being able to run wild.

A person assisting Nemon in Altgard's Safe Haven. He has a long-standing relationship with Nemon, trusts her, feels a personal bond, and actively tries to help. Although he never ascended as a Daeva, he is a skilled warrior unafraid of facing danger. Despite his rough appearance, he has a warm and loyal nature, attracting many followers and maintaining strong connections.

A Spirit drawn by the energy of Ardus Shrine.
In a dazed state, it has the faint purpose of guarding the Ardus Shrine.
A Drakan of the Nahid Brigade who manages the Drana Plantation.

Perk is a special Varg born with a huge and strong body. The Varg swore loyalty to the Balaur, so Perk was also destined to become a soldier serving the Balaur, but Perk's mind was very unstable. Eventually, it took the combined efforts of his tribe and multiple Drakan to subdue him during a rampage. Santras felt interested in Perk and, instead of disposing of him, brought him to Dranactus Dungeon. Since then, Santras has kept Perk as a special prisoner and made him his toy.

A fire spirit that was a minion of the fire Daeva Agnita. After Kromede took control of the Fire Temple, it followed Kromede's commands. Currently, it guards the Fire Temple, following the orders of the Mirror of Desire which has consumed Kromede. Due to its massive body and overwhelming strength, it is also known as the Fire Giant.

A manifestation of Zumion's Relic, the Warding Feather, which is located in the Zumion Relic Storage, in human form. Blessed by the ancient Daeva <QK>Zumion</>, who was beloved by the gods, its appearance resembles Zumion. It hopes that the relic's power will be used for Verteron, as Zumion wished. It was ordered to test those who would break the seal and only release the relic's power to those who prove worthy.
An Aullaeu pursuing berserkers or exiles expelled from Aullaeu Village.

A guard of <Queen Karat> located in the dungeon <Karat's Nest> in the ruins area of the Abyss.
Protects the surroundings while the queen spawns.

A Wind Spirit that has existed in Altamia Highland for a long time.
After Kaisinel became extinct, it lost reason and became violent.

A Ranger of the Dawn Legion active in Verteron. He lived as a mercenary with his only blood relative, his older brother, but the mercenary company was wiped out and he lost his brother. After wandering alone, he joined the Dawn Legion at Caelid's invitation. Although he had a wary personality, he has opened his heart to some extent after spending a long time with the Dawn Legion. He can be prickly at times, but he is very affectionate and thinks of Caelid as a brother.

To halt the advance of the "Dragon Lords," the Empyrean Lords poured all of their remaining power into raising a "Bulwark."
Through Zikel's desperate resistance, and at the cost of their own extinction, they succeeded.

Yet this Bulwark, raised atop the sacrifice of so many souls, proved only a temporary measure, and the world beyond the Bulwark's protection remained under the Balaur's dominion.
As a fragment carrying AION's will, you must ascend through the memories left by the beings of the Eternal Dream and gain the power to restore Atreia.

The Monoliths of the Empyrean Lords contain their power and serve various functions. Among them, a representative function is sealing the Empyrean Lord's sanctums or relics. Only the Empyrean Lords' direct Cavalier soldiers can properly use the Monoliths. In the case of Zikel's Monolith, the Destruction Archons who follow Zikel can properly understand and utilize the Monolith's functions.

When the terrified people of Altgard buried the Karas, not only the Karas but also innocent people were sacrificed. Giselle, an ordinary maiden from Altgard who loved to sing, was also an innocent victim who was buried alive, despite not being Karas. Separated from her beloved, Giselle was trapped alive in an underground grave and died, becoming a vengeful wraith filled with injustice and sorrow. Even after becoming a wraith, she cannot leave the music box given by her lover, wandering around it. The lyrics she hummed before her death now escape as sobs.

A Cleric of the Dawn Legion active in Verteron. She had been captured by the Balaur and taken to Nahid Fortress when Caelid rescued her and later joined the Dawn Legion. She trusts Caelid absolutely and positively accepts and follows Caelid's reckless operations such as the attack on Poeta. With a kind and positive personality, she brightens the atmosphere of the Dawn Legion. She encourages the Dawn Legionnaires without losing hope even in difficult situations.

A Drakan from Meslamtaeda's special forces, the Seker Strike Forces. Sandha operates independently to spy on and disrupt Daeva. He has the ability to create territories within with he can move unseen using the powers granted by Meslamtaeda. Normal Daeva cannot detect him, but those with a "Daeva Sense" can find his tracks.
Since Sandha finds humans and Daeva interesting and enjoys observing and analyzing their behavior, he does not hastily massacre humans and Daeva, unlike other Balaurs. Sandha primarily conducts surveillance and espionage missions around Daeva strongholds and takes great pleasure in his work.

The Brigade High Commander of the Dawn Legion active in Verteron. He has been fighting fiercely against the Balaur since the Bulwark's appearance in Elysea. At one point, he led the largest Legion in Verteron and stood at the forefront of the Balaur resistance as the representative of the Elyos allied forces. However, about a year ago, after being defeated in the assault on Nahid Fortress in alliance with the Notos Legion and others, Caelid decided that there was no chance of winning the battle against the Balaur and focused on going beyond the Bulwark. Upon learning that Phernos, who came from beyond the Bulwark, had been captured and taken to Poeta, he executed a dangerous operation to rescue him.

Bakarma was a legion commander under the extinct Dragon Lord Beritra. When Atreia was swept up in tectonic shifts during the Last War, the Bakarma Brigade and Draupnir Cave were sucked into the Abyss. While wandering the Abyss, Bakarma encountered an unknown power in Atreia and realized that this power would lead him to become a greater being. Bakarma denied his identity as a Balaur who had to pursue slaughter and desire only to become a Dragon Lord and sought a new path of transcendence.

A dream afterimage that reflects a part of Siel, one of AION's two guardians and the Empyrean Lord who governs time. Siel sacrificed herself during the Great Catastrophe to prevent the collapse of the tower. Even after Siel perished, her memories remained in AION's dream. Siel, who became a dream afterimage, still feels compassion for AION's creations and seeks to guide Atreia on the right path.

The Altgard branch manager of the Quai Merchant Guild. The Quai Merchant Guild is a historically significant Shugo merchant group in Asmodae, which dominated trade in southern Altgard even after the Last War. However, they have now been driven to the outskirts, having lost the Gribade mines mining rights and their Merchant's Port of Call to the Steel Hammer Merchants, which is allied with the Balaur. They await the day they can restore Quai's reputation. They are proud, but intelligent, and they recognize Nemon's skills, trying to maximize their gains.

A high-ranking executive of the Blades operating in Morheim. As Gerod's confidant, he actively assisted in the founding of the Blades by providing funds. Like Gerod, he was a scion of a noble family in Asmodae, but he caused problems with his cruel behavior from an early age, making him a nuisance to the family. After becoming active in the Blades, he actively committed many cruel acts as if he had found his true calling. He is deeply obsessed with the power of Fafnite. He is aware of Gerod's obsession with Nemon and participates in Gerod's tormenting of Nemon.

A soul of a Temple Protector Legion centurion who fought against the Balaur forces of Meslamtaeda when Zumion Shrine was cursed in ancient times.
So much time has passed that he has forgotten who he is.

One of the members of the Blades.
He enjoys bullying the weak. He has little interest in Gerod's actions or Fafnite. He is a typical outlaw Daeva who joined the Blades to indulge in destruction and slaughter.

Daeva are born from humans and grow to resemble them, but those destined to become Daeva possess exceptional abilities from an early age. Through a pivotal event or trial, they "ascend," fully awakening their potential, and allowing them to use Odyle energy freely.

The key evidence of a Daeva are their wings and their ability to fly. Ever since the collapse of AION, their powers have weakened. They need to find the fragments of AION in order to reclaim their forgotten power.

To halt the advance of the "Dragon Lords," the Empyrean Lords poured all of their remaining power into raising a "Bulwark."
Through Zikel's desperate resistance, and at the cost of their own extinction, they succeeded.

Yet this Bulwark, raised atop the sacrifice of so many souls, proved only a temporary measure, and the world beyond the Bulwark's protection remained under the Balaur's dominion.
As a fragment carrying AION's will, you must ascend through the memories left by the beings of the Eternal Dream and gain the power to restore Atreia.

A Daeva who fiercely fought against the Balaur in life.
He resisted for a long time even when Ishtar took and transformed him into a Sura.
He was made an example after becoming a Sura and now wanders Altamia Highland.

A mineral containing Odyle, it emits a mysterious Odyle light. Due to the power of Odyle, many creatures in Atreia are drawn to Odylium. The Krall, in particular, favor Odylium, establishing and utilizing mines. After the Last War, as Odyle became scarce, Daeva also began using Odylium actively, making it rarer than before.
A fierce beast of the Moslan Forest. It was not ferocious in the past, but now it is a target for subjugation. It has eaten many beasts and people.

A fire spirit that was a minion of the fire Daeva Agnita. After Kromede took control of the Fire Temple, it followed Kromede's commands. Currently, it guards the Fire Temple, following the orders of the Mirror of Desire which has consumed Kromede. It controls flames freely and can burn even distant enemies.

A member of the Hugo Mercenaries, a mercenary of ordinary skill commonly seen anywhere in Altgard. He longed for Hugo's recognition but never earned it, leading to a growing sense of inferiority and boasted about a paradise beyond the Bulwark. Kraki accepted the Blood Blades' offer, betrayed the Hugo Mercenaries in Ishalgen, and stole the High Priest's Fafnite. The rewards the Blood Blades promised Kraki were unknown. However, Kraki did not receive the desired rewards and was killed after being used as bait to lure Nemon by the Blood Blades.

It was armor personally blessed by the Empyrean Lord Zikel and bestowed upon the Destruction Archon. When a Destruction Archon wearing this armor perished, the next Destruction Archon inherited it. When it became too worn to function as armor, it was stored in the Destruction Archon Underground Fortress. Although all the Destruction Archons are gone, the wills of the Archons reside in the armor. Notun considers itself the Destruction Archon guarding the underground fortress and believes it is its duty to protect it.

Born from Fafnir's blood, it possesses a portion of Fafnir's power. It has almost no reason, but it remembers only the missions given by Fafnir. The Poison Blood's mission is to contaminate the forests of Altgard and wither the Sacred Tree Grisilla to death. Faithfully carrying out its mission, the Poison Blood dried up Grisilla's roots and was on the verge of achieving its goal of killing Grisilla.

These are fragments of AION's dream. They have fallen all over Atreia, and each fragment is guarded by a protector. Only those who have the potential to become an Arch Daeva can discover, activate them, and read the information contained within the fragments.

Daeva are born from humans and grow to resemble them, but those destined to become Daeva possess exceptional abilities from an early age. Through a pivotal event or trial, they "ascend," fully awakening their potential, and allowing them to use Odyle energy freely.

The key evidence of a Daeva are their wings and their ability to fly. Ever since the collapse of AION, their powers have weakened. They need to find the fragments of AION in order to reclaim their forgotten power.

These birds were summoned by the Aullaeu shamans of the Urugugu tribe borrowing the power of Dragon Lord Ishtar. These birds are believed to embody the Core of the Aullaeu and serve as their protectors. Summoning an Aultross requires at least three shamans, and summoning a higher-rank bird demands even more shamans and offerings.

A tome inscribed with Spirit magic, created by Kaisinel, the Seeker of Intelligence and Bearer of Fear, yet forbidden due to its dangers. Even after it was declared a banned book, countless replicas and counterfeits spread, and fearless Spiritmasters attempted to wield the magic within. However, the original Scarlotus may only be read by the High Priest of Illusion. Among the spells recorded in Scarlotus, there is said to be a forbidden magic capable of resurrecting the dead by replacing their souls with Spirits.

The Urugugu tribe has worshiped the Red Dragon as a god since ancient times. Although the Dragon Lord they worship has changed from Tiamat to the current Ishtar, the fact that it is the Red Dragon remains unchanged. The altar for worshiping the Red Dragon is a sacred place for the Aullaeu and is heavily guarded by defenders. Aulak is the leader of the defenders who protect the altar and a strong warrior. However, Aulak has also been transformed and lost himself under Reda's magic.
A researcher in charge of the area that creates modified weapons using Drana at the Nahid Brigade Stronghold.

Arch Daeva are shattered Fragments of AION, a great being of the universe, and thus, all Arch Daeva shall return to perfection by collecting the fragments and become complete once more. The Ascension Artifact lets its owner absorb other Arch Daeva to reach AION.

Those who swear the oath and overcome the trial shall rise as Arch Daeva, and ascend higher as they absorb the fate and abyss of other Arch Daeva.

A Krall brainwashed to follow the Balaur.
Still possesses knowledge and power of the Tursin Krall's sorcery and exerts influence over other Krall.

An apparition that holds a part of the memory and power of Zikel, the God of Destruction, Gladiators, and Templars. Zikel lost most of his power when he erected the Bulwark in Asmodae but protected Altgard with the Destruction Archons. Deeming that he could no longer stop Fafnir, he created a Blood Barrier in Impetusium, sacrificing himself and the lives of the Destruction Archons. Zikel disappeared, but a remnant of his apparition still remains within the Blood Barrier, protecting the Core of the Destruction. The apparition resembles Zikel in lifetime, and his thoughts and speech are similar. However, the apparition is only a very small part of Zikel's existence.

A holy animal of Cantas Valley.
It is native to the western Cantas Valley. Since the collapse of the AION Tower, it has been hostile to Daeva.

An Aullaeu merchant of the Urugugu tribe. He secretly continued trading with Daeva or Shugos if it meant making money. Currently, under Aulamus's orders, he contacted the Astin Mercenaries to capture Kochi. Of course, securing Kochi is only a secondary goal; Duduri's true aim is to make a financial profit.

1. Character-based data is transferred along with Quna and Mileage, while server-based data of current server is reset.
- Account-based data, such as shop and content usage counts, are applied across all servers and are therefore unaffected by server transfer.

2. Non-Transferrable Content
- Server-based cash shop purchase history is not transferred.
- Items or currencies in the storage are not transferred.
- Mailbox is not transferred.
- Market contents are not transferred.
- Character slots are not transferred.
- Last 10 match history for Arena and Battlefield is reset.

3. Current/Target Server Synchronized Content
- NPC Shops: Server-based purchase counts are adjusted based on current server.
- Weekly Cumulative Play Rewards: Play Counts and Odyle Energy Cube Kina Gain are adjusted based on current server.
- Server-Based Content: Daily Dungeon / Shugo Festival / Dimensional Invasion / Remaining Unclaimed Cube Count / Sprout Badge Reward Count are adjusted based on current server.
- Substance Morph: Server-based morph counts are adjusted based on current server.
- Personal Trades: Daily trades are adjusted based on current server.

4. Individually-Applied Content
- Attendance: Server-based attendance is transferred with the character, while the current server's attendance is reset. The target server's attendance is reset and the current server's attendance progress is applied.
- Subscriptions: Transfer with characters, while the current server is reset. Remaining subscription period is added to the target server.
- Membership Pass: Transfer with characters, while the current server is reset. Active membership passes on the current server will be treated as completed and the rewards will be delivered. Pending passes on the current server will be added to the target server.
- Daeva Pass: Transfer with characters, while the current server is reset. When transferring a character that has purchased a server-based Daeva Pass, the purchase count will be added to the target server and removed from the current server.
- Growth Support: Transfers with characters, while the current server is reset.
- Daily Duty Quest Progress Count: When transferring a character with Duty quests in progress, the character's progress count will be added to the target server and removed from the current server. When the transferred counts are added to the target server, the combined number may exceed the maximum.
- Achievements: Transfer with characters, while the current server is reset. Server-based achievements are compared between both servers and then set to the higher levels. Server-based achievement rewards can only be obtained if they are unclaimed in both servers.
- Pet Achievements: Pet-related achievements are the only exception and are preserved on both servers. Current and target server achievements are combined and applied to both servers.
- Closet: Transfers with characters and is added together, and the current server is reset. Collection Effect is applied based on the combined result.
- Pets: Transfer with characters and are added together, and the current server is reset. Pets that reach max level will have XP converted into Soul Crystals. Owned Effects and Collection Effects will be applied based on the combined results. Collection status rewards can only be obtained if they are unclaimed in both servers. You can choose to apply Genus Insight from either the current or target server, but regardless of which one is selected, Genus Insight from the current server is reset. Duplicate Special pets purchased with cash or Quna will be replaced for Pet Exchange Tickets, and duplicate Special pets purchased from the Pass Shop will be replaced with Daeva Pass Shop Coin: Returning.
- Season Missions: Transfer with characters, while the current server is reset. Shared season missions on the target server are reset and the current server's progress is applied.
- Theostones: Transfer with characters and are added together, and the current server is reset.
- Empyrean Trace Resonance: Transfers with characters, but is also preserved on the current server. Current and target server Empyrean Trace resonance data are combined and applied to both servers.
- Server Storage Expansion Slots: Server Storage expansion slots on the current server are preserved. Server Storage expansion slots compared between servers and the higher amount will be applied to the target server.
- Coin Shops: The current server's purchase history is preserved. Purchase history is compared between both servers and the higher value is applied to the target server.

[Crafting System Overview]

- Crafting uses separate success and failure gauges.
- When crafting, each time the success or failure gauge increases is called a "turn".
- The result of each turn is calculated independently.
- If the success gauge reaches the target first, crafting succeeds, but if the failure gauge reaches the target first, crafting fails.
- However, if you are attacked while crafting is in progress, crafting will be canceled and result in failure.
- Each recipe has different gauge target and increase values, so the rates of success also vary.
- Gauge increase values correlate to the difference between your character's Proficiency Level and the recipe's Proficiency Level, and therefore affect your maximum chances of crafting success.
- When normal crafting succeeds, COMBO recipe crafting may be attempted based on COMBO activation chance.

[Success Chance Information]

- The [Expected Probability] tab shows the maximum probability of success based on the difference with the current recipe's Proficiency Level.
- The probability is rounded up to six decimal places.
- The displayed probability is calculated using recipe gauge information, Proficiency Level adjustments, and any other factors that affect the probability of crafting success.
- To view COMBO recipe success chances, press the "Change" button in the [Expected Probability] tab to switch between base probability and COMBO probability.

A library built in Altamia Canyon by the librarian Hypatia. Fearing it would be attacked and the accumulated knowledge within lost, she distributed the books across multiple other libraries.

A fortress that served as an Abyss Gate and repelled invaders into Verteron. It was destroyed and rebuilt many times during the long war with the Balaur, but was eventually abandoned altogether once Daeva had grown too thin. It is now garrisoned and managed by Krall.

The body of High Priest Hystan, whose soul and mind were stolen by Fafnite, wandered through Altgard, slaughtering countless innocents in its wake.

When Hystan’s body finally reached Moslan Forest, the Nornir summoned the Daeva and sealed it away. To honor the victims, they erected a stele that preserves the truth of High Priest Hystan’s fate, and offerings are still made there in remembrance of those who were lost.
An altar in a cave made by a Fire Temple worshiper. Though it once held ancient tomes revering the Fire Temple, it has been abandoned after an Artifact Fragment fell.
A <QK>western camp</> base located in the west of Chaotic Middle Reshanta.
The main base of a Taytra Brigade Kurpak unit under Sigebert's command. The unit is made up of swift and decisive soldiers that can be deployed anywhere in Iralcig Highland and Muspel Volcano Zone.

Gerod, leader of the Blades, after augmenting his body with Fafnite.

Through his studies of Fafnite, he discovered its power to harness the souls within and use them to strengthen his own body. Yet the transformation came at a cost. Once his form had fully mutated, even he could no longer return to his original Daeva state.

This tower stands at the site where Deltras, the Elyos Daeva, was executed.
After lying abandoned for some time, it is now used by the fake Fate Archons to imprison internal dissidents and those Fate Archons who refused to submit to High Priest Sigebert.
A temporary base for Indnath, who has been chasing Nemon ever since the Lagta Fortress in Altgard. The base is meant to accommodate his forces temporarily until they can eliminate Nemon.
A small pond on the Tranein Highland.
A cave where a passage to the unstable Abyss has appeared. It contains additional information about the Ancient City of Ru.

A passageway connecting the forest area below Anturn Cliff and the village of Alder.
For some reason, passage is prohibited.

A secret base set up by Chloris's band belowground in the Fractured Land.
After Chloris's group discovered the existence of the Lepharists' culvert, they have been working on creating a tunnel leading to it.
The underground part of the fallen Verteron Fortress. It is used by the Krall as their residence.

A campsite located between Kromede's Island and Patamor Village.
It is located beneath a small hill that just barely blocks the blizzards that blow behind it.
Kromede's followers cannot give it up due to it being the best hub for quick travel through the snowfield.
A hideout for Daeva who betrayed the Notos Legion. Instead of fighting the Balaur, they now ambush and rob pilgrims on the road. The looted supplies are piled throughout the hideout.

This Oracle was built within Uruthumheim and used extensively by the Three Women of Fate—Skuld, Urd, and Verdandi.
Distressed by the gradual loss of their power to see fate as AION grew weaker and weaker, they built this oracle and locked themselves away within in search of glimpses of Atreia's future.
Unable to read the fate of Atreia in its entirety as they used to, they decided to go their separate ways in search of their own methods for discerning Atreia's future.
Following its abandonment, the Oracle was partially destroyed by Dredgion bombardment, but the most important spaces survived, with traps in place to prevent the Balaur and outlaws from trespassing.
A hideout where the surviving true Fate Archons once stayed. Pledging their eternal loyalty to their Empyrean Lord and High Priest, these Archons met their end here, unable to escape.
A secret place where Steel Hammer Merchants Crobakhi hid his coins

A landing spot for Dredgion, the flying battleships of the Balaur used for transport and bombarding Daeva.
Destroy the Balaur base and annihilate their forces and commanders.

Krao Cave is rich in a special mineral called Krao, known for its ability to repel external forces.
Lepharists conducted various experiments with Krao here and, during the Last War, created the powerful Berk, which played a key role in the conflict.
But when Berk went berserk and lost control, the Lepharists sealed the cave and withdrew.
Quarters where Muqaka, the Chief of Black Claw Village, resides. All Fafnite production and trade statements, among other important documents, are kept in his quarters.

A Lepharist worshiper of Atheron.
As an imperfect Daeva that cannot use his wings, he has dreamed of becoming a complete Daeva since before the fall of AION.
In order undergo Atheron's surgical treatments, he did the Lepharists' dirty work, gave up all belongings, and even forsook his own family.
Eventually, he receive enhancement procedures that gave him powers beyond those of a Daeva, although he has lost everything else.
A secret library built in Tolbas Forest by the librarian Hypatia to preserve the knowledge of the Elyos.

The western expanse of the broad plains in the heart of Eltnen. It is considerably drier than it was in the past, but the land is still tinged with verdance dating back to when the Lacephin Mystic Spring was brimming with life.
A base of the Spirit Guides who remain to aid in the recovery of the Spirit Isle. It also serves as a forward base for those exploring the island.
Habitat of the Holyaul who barely makes a living on the outskirts of the forest.

Drawn by its rich veins of Odylium—a rarity in Odyle-depleted Verteron—, this cave is crawling with Sura who escaped the Nahid's Brigade's laboratories. Though it boasts a vault filled with treasures of long-dead Daeva, many of which contain Odylium, few dare approach due to the Sura threat.

A keep once held by the Fate Archons who worshipped Empyrean Lord Marchutan in the past.
Despite being severely damaged by a volcanic eruption, Marchutan and his Fate Archons made their stand against the Balaur here.
Now, it is a base for Sigebert's machinations.
A subspace created for flight training.
The cliffs of the Cantas Valley feature natural caves of various shapes and sizes, favored as hideouts by the many poachers who ply their illicit trade in and around the valley.
A powerful impact split the floating island that once housed the fortress into two. This is the southern island.

A historic village that has existed in Ishalgen since ancient times.
Even now, when the Balaur have taken over Ishalgen, the Daeva still reside here.

The remains of a temple attached to the Destruction Archon Fortress. The building is completely destroyed, and only a few broken stone statues remain. In the center, there is a half-broken stele inscribed with the Archon Oath.
A rugged territory south of the Mahindel River, which splits Altgard into north and south. Outlaws are currently occupying the area and are extending the reach of their power.
The northern part of Tolbas Forest, adjacent to the Verteron Fortress Ruins. Dangerous animals and plants can be found here.
Root of the Sacred Tree Entrance

A mysterious cave with a hidden entrance by the lake.
There is a legend that Daeva sought it out in the past in order to ascend.

Armor once worn by the Destruction Archons, imbued with their indomitable fighting spirit and the power of Empyrean Lord Zikel, who personally blessed and bestowed it. Though its wearer is long gone, the armor still believes itself to be a soldier defending the Underground Fortress. It regards all who approach as intruders, leaving no possibility for communication.
A camp for Shulak laborers. It is also used to mine and load the surrounding Fafnite gemstones. The mined gemstones and carts are scattered around.
A place of rest for the Kobolds laboring at the Drana Plantation. Some de-brainwashed Kobolds pretend to be brainwashed in order to try and escape.

Land linking the plains of northern Eltnen with the southern deserts. Normal plants cannot grow in this desolate area, so only wild Drana coats the ground with red.
The Lepharist Researcher Center that serves as their headquarters is located here as well, so they use the local Drana for various research.
The mutant byproducts are carelessly released on to the Fractured Land.

A canyon occupied by the Urugugu Tribe of Aullaeu who worship Ishtar, the Crimson Dragon Lord. The Urugugu village and altar are hidden inside the canyon.
Urugugu Canyon is guarded by Auldor, a sacred bird summoned by Urugugu Shamans using Ishtar's power.
An outpost garrisoned by the Dratona troops who monitor the Drana Plantation.
The miasma grows stronger with each passing day in a cave choked with poisonous plants. Within, the number of Agrints and slimes corrupted by the vegetation continues to rise.

An underground prison operated by the Balaur in the Dranactus region.
Savage beasts roam the surrounding area to keep an eye on the inmates, while the structure itself contains numerous facilities for imprisoning and torturing Daeva who oppose the Balaur, squeezing any information that will help them eradicate the local Legions
Captured Daeva are forced into labor, and turned into Fafnite when they are of no use.

A temple where Fate Archon candidates once trained and studied Marchutan’s scriptures. Following the massacre of the instructors and candidates by Sigebert’s loyalists, the site is now haunted by vengeful souls who guard the temple's treasures from outsiders.

An Abyss Gate once located above Verteron Fortress. When the Fortress fell, the gate was also attacked and destroyed. An Abyss Rift appeared for a time afterward, but has now subsided. Klaw from the Abyss Rift have settled in the area.
A small Shugo base located in the northern Tolbas Forest. It stands along the path leading to the Wind Breeze Merchants HQ.
A secret armory of the Guardians who resisted the Balaur to the last. No one knows if there are still any useful weapons.
The eastern region of the Cantas Valley. Groups of refugees attempting to flee to the Dawn Legion often pass through. The area is relatively dangerous due to the lack of Dawn Legion presence.
The place where Spatalos, former high commander of the Verteron Legion, sealed away Vamana, a vanguard captain of the Drakan. According to folklore, the echoes of their battle can still be heard.

The Creion are a research group founded by Noiran, a genius engineer from the Lepharist Revolutionaries. In the hopes of saving a world with rapidly dwindling Odyle reserves, they successfully synthesized an alternative to Odyle energy.
However, the new energy proved dangerously unstable and catastrophic. Realizing the consequences of her work, Noiran abandoned the project and sealed the laboratory herself.
Not everyone agreed with her decision. The more radical members of the Creion infiltrated the abandoned facility and continued the research, conducting horrific experiments on living beings.
Over time, their original purpose faded into obscurity. Now they live only to carry out their endless experiments, consumed by obsession and madness.

An island located in a remote corner of the Atreian seas.
After the Great Catastrophe, tectonic shifts in the area of the island caused a massive amount of Fafnite Gemstones in the water to shatter and smash into the island with great force.
This resulted in a massive ordeal for the flora and fauna of the island. Organisms that were poisoned by the Fafnite Gemstones lost their minds or shriveled up, until eventually only those who managed to adapt by expelling the Azure Breath were left.

A hideout Verdandi stayed in when she came to Morheim with Skuld—before she settled in Patamor Village. Now, the area is occupied by Indnath's forces, who have been chasing Nemon all the way from Altgard.
The main base of the Lagta Brigade, who rule over Altgard under High Commander Lagta. The base periodically sends Fafnite to Ishalgen and Morheim.

A coastline comprised of steep cliffs, and the only way to enter the island without being detected by the Balaur.
The Dawn Legion infiltrated Poeta via these cliffs during their operation to rescue Phernos.

A secret library built by the librarian Musein to preserve the knowledge of the Asmodians, under the sworn protection of the Kerubar. Whispers tell of ancient tomes containing information on the Bulwark.
A site of pilgrimage where worshippers of Kaisinel stop and write devotionals. Popularized by a legend that he once stayed here briefly, it is now home only to lost spirits.

A place where Life Daeva once nurtured life itself in the distant past, now occupied by scholars researching the ruins and refugees with nowhere else to go.
The scholars researching this site have not been deterred by the threat posed by the suspicious forces visiting the area.

A mass of coagulated blood that fell from the body of Dragon Lord Fafnir, twisted into a poisonous, sentient abomination. It lashes out with sticky tendrils, attacking by spewing toxic blood at its prey. Left unchecked, it absorbs nearby blood clots to grow ever larger and more powerful.

A sky island floating on the outskirts of Elysea, rich in Odyle ever since its creation.
As Odyle depleted, an imbalance formed between the island and the ground below, giving rise to a colossal Odyle Storm that engulfed the skies around it, and only recently was a way discovered to pierce through the storm and reach the island's heart.
The storm has kept the island untouched, maintaining the original environment from before AION's collapse, dominated by diverse flora infused with Odyle.
A Nahid Brigade Fortress under Dragon Lord Ishtar. This place also works as a bio-research station, with facilities for the confinement and study of the Daeva.

A street stall set up by Shulak trading in the looted goods from the Basfelt Ruins. Despite its small size, it is popular for its wide range of products and willingness to obtain rare items for an extra price.
An area where the Dredgion of the Fafnir Brigade crashed after being caught in the Abyss Rift accident. The surrounding soil is heavily contaminated with waste fluids from the ship.
A place to store the Aullaeu's belongings. Pinos, Aullaeu's minions, serve as laborers.
An ancient armory of the Destruction Archons, dutifully guarded by their kin throughout the ages. Rumors speak of a hidden treasure concealed deep within its depths.

A mindscape through which AION's wisdom flows, where the consciousnesses of all beings on Atreia converge and the mystical artifacts that govern AION's dreams can be found. All information from the past, present, and future flows through this sacred space, and only those with the power of AION can access it.

An area where desertification has progressed slower than usual due to the Life Daeva's operations and water management here in the distant past. A greenbelt remains from that time, though not as large as the Ruberein Highland.
When an object fell from the sky several years ago and devastasted the hillside, a suspicious group clad in white appeared, searching for something and stirring up chaos.

A group of bandits have set up camp at the bottom of Altamia Canyon after the illusionary enchantment that protected Zumion Village and the canyon was removed. Aware of the patrol schedule of the Notos Legion, they time their raids on Zumion Village carefully.
The southern part of Tolbas Forest, and a popular hiding place for bandits and marauders.
A Blades hideout hidden below Idun's Lake. It was previously a sanctum for Daeva that followed Azphel.
A Balaur research base dedicated to transforming Daeva into Sura.

A town established by Shulak of the Steel Hammer Merchants.
It was originally a base for the Quai Merchant Guild, and a port that boasted a status as the logistical center of Altgard, with a steady stream of airships carrying goods from the Abyss and across Asmodae. It has since been taken over by the Steel Hammer Merchants, collaborators with the Balaur.

A site where a small legion resisting the Balaur was annihilated. Daeva soldiers whose bodies and souls have been split now wander aimlessly. The Balaur intend to seal these specters within the ruins and repurpose them into an immortal brigade.
Archipelago of Siel's Wings - Siel's Left Wing

The sanctum of Zikel, Empyrean Lord of Destruction, and home base of the Destruction Archons. A major battlefield during the Balaur invasion, it is now largely destroyed and abandoned. None dare visit due to rumors that Empyrean Lord Zikel went mad and wiped out all of the Archons.
A secret vault bult by modifying a natural cave, used by the Blades to hide looted treasures and Odyle.

Ishtar developed a technology called Surana capable of extracting the life force of Daeva and converting it into alternative energy. To facilitate research and development, numerous groups of Balaur dedicated themselves to systematically hunting Daeva and other lifeforms for use as experimental subjects, imprisoning them in nearby bases and supplying them to Nahid Brigade Fortress whenever needed.

The Fafnite ore smelted in this massive forge is mounted onto Fafnium to absorb the souls of Daeva.
Eliminate the forge commanders to neutralize the facility.
Land used by the Balaur to raise Drana for their food supply. Drana has stained the entire area red, with Balaur and their minions wherever one looks.
The ground beneath Altgard is weakening due to underground tunnels used by the burrowing insectoid. It is said the burrowing insectoids dwell in this cave.

Once the ruins of an ancient Daeva's residence, it became inaccessible after the impact of the Awakening Artifact's fall destroyed the entrance.
High Priest Sigebert recently set up a device allowing him to go inside and search for the Artifact.
One of the Lagta Brigade's Fafnite Storages, overseen by the Supervisor Sinah.

A Daeva hiding from the Balaur once cast a spell on the Manduri here for protection. However, the flawed spell caused the Manduri to become exceedingly aggressive. The Daeva fled, leaving only these furious creatures behind.
(Temp) An area held by the Taytra Brigade under Fafnir's command. The territory includes the Mistmane Stronghold and Taytra Fortress.
An area of floating rocks or remains of fortresses destroyed in the Last War. It is the closest area to the western camp base and is relatively easy to access from the base by gliding.

During the Karas massacres, not even the nobles could escape their fate. Altgard's slaughterers rounded up the noble families suspected of being Karas, confined them within a single ossuary, and left them imprisoned there.

The Aullaeu worshipped Dragon Lord Tiamat for generations. Even following her fall and the ascendance of Dragon Lord Ishtar, they did not falter in their worship, and continue to dedicate altars to her.
A natural cave between the cliffs of Basfelt Ruins. Graverobbers, fleeing from the Blades, hide here.

A campsite located in Western Cantas Valley, used by the Dawn Legion for Odyle collection.
Legion members and assisting Shugo merchants reside here.

A Drakan member of Meslamtaeda's Seker Strike Force who operates alone to spy on and sabotage Daeva, using power inherited from Meslamtaeda to hide himself away in realms of his own creation. Normal Daeva cannot detect him, but those blessed with "Daeva Sense" may use it to uncover his tracks.

Unabashedly cruel, Zrash relishes in slaughter, with an undisciplined selfishness that caused him to be transferred from the Assassination Squad after causing no end of trouble. He finds great satisfaction in the solitude of his current job hunting down Daeva, but is often frustrated at his inability to rampage as wildly as he would like.

A hideout of wanted criminals who originally worked for the Steel Hammer Merchants until they were caught smuggling goods. Now settled in the Eastern Gribade Highland, they continue to target passing merchants.

A ritualist who guarded the Aullaeu Altar.

He resisted Reda's mind-controlling magic until the very end, choosing to end his own life rather than succumb to her influence.

Aulisa's corpse, left upon the altar, mutated and became part of a tree root during resurrection.
The resting place of Kraka, a legendary chieftain of the Tursin Krall. The Krall worship him still—building altars and offering tribute.

As Eltnen suffered relentless invasions by the Balaur and the Lepharists, many Daeva became part of the ever-growing list of casualties. Tifus, a Life Daeva, secretly moved the bodies of the fallen to a secluded cavern in the hopes that his kin could return to AION's embrace.
However, AION's fall made it impossible for the dead to return to Odyle. Instead, they rotted within the cave, mutating into vile contaminations.
Tifus, who sought only to grant his fellow Daeva their final rest, succumbed to the contamination as well.
Burdened by resentment and unable to return to Odyle, he remains forever entombed within the dark cavern as a revenant.

A floating island that broke away during the collapse of the Arkanis Sky Temple, now serving as a Balaur sky outpost. It is overseen by Dinakra, a Balaur who is content with his rank of outpost captain and has little interest in pursuing greater power.

An underground tomb that has been reduced to a testing site for disturbing necromancy.
Eliminate the necromancers performing forbidden rituals and their twisted experimental creations.
A sky island covered in twisted thorn trees that are corrupted by Drana. Its symbolic position at the center of the upper layer has earned it the name of <QK>Red Thorn Crown Isle</>.

A snowfield containing an ancient ruin called the Executioner's Tower.
A long time ago, Zikel executed the Storm Legion in this very place, triggering the start of the Elyos-Asmodian War.
It is equally as harsh a territory as the volcanoes of Muspel, to Kromede's followers.
A fortress built by Dragon Lord Fafnir after he conquered Ishalgen, garrisoned by his army and used to store Fafnite, which steal and imprison the souls of Daeva.

A temporary campsite once used by the Dawn Legion while assisting with the restoration of the Barrier Tower.
It is no longer in use, as the Legion is no longer involved in the restoration.

When the Ishtar Legion laid waste to Eltnen, the Life Daeva paid a heavy toll in blood. Those who survived withdrew to hidden outposts, quietly working to restore their ruined home.
But as the Lepharists invaded, the last of the Life Daeva were forced into hiding and ultimately disappeared.
Though this cave once sheltered them, it now stands empty and forgotten, stripped of its original purpose.

A place where the memories of the vanished Elyos Empyrean Lord <QK>Kaisinel</> remain as fragments of dreams. Though little more than a dream, the Empyrean Lord's power over fear remains vibrant, and he has no mercy for the Asmodians he detests so much.

A base for legionnaire outlaws. They attempted to raid Zumion Village, but were repelled by the Notos Legion and ended up settling here. They make a living looting supplies traveling to and from the highland and raid Notos Legion bases.

He proved himself worthy to become AION and was the closest to ever reach it, but now known as the fragment that failed to become AION.
Unable to escape the abyss inside himself and the fate that has found him, he is cursed to wait for another Arch Daeva inside his broken dreams.

A hilly area scorched by the eruption of a volcano in Muspel. Asmodians once flourished on the fertile farmlands here, but now only faint traces of that time remain.
Located between the coast and volcanoes, the vegetation is quite unique.
A former crematorium, but abandoned since the Karas Massacre. It is now occasionally used by gravekeepers to store supplies.

A high-ranking member of the Lepharists, devoted follower and right-hand officer to <QK>Atheron</>.
She hasn't received any of Atheron's enhancement procedures because she considers her to be inadequate and incapable of living up to his ideals, but she is willing to sacrifice herself on his way to godhood.

A memorial where the Nornir Priestess Soirel and the faithful once honored the memories of the dead. Their rites came to a tragic end when a sudden Balaur attack claimed the souls of all who had gathered there. Since then, the memorial has stood abandoned, unmaintained and unvisited.
A place where an ancient Zumion Priestess sealed herself away together with Meslamtaeda's poison, enduring intense agony as she continues her solitary battle.
The main base of a bandit group occupying Calderon Canyon. They expanded their power using illegal explosives and now pillage anyone in sight, human or Shugo alike.
After being defeated by Ishtar's armies, some Daeva suffered extinction, some became Sura, and some even became Apparitions. The wrathful screams of those Daeva Apparitions are heard day and night.

A base for members of the Nahid Brigade patrolling the Kraka Footpath, with a particular focus on the direction of Zumion Village. It also serves as a hub for gathering small amounts of Drana generated in the outskirts and transporting it in bulk to the Nahid Brigade's main force.
A cave where a rift to the unstable Abyss has appeared. It contains information about the secrets of the Ancient City of Ru.
A place where the Norst Legion and the Daeva are staying to dominate the Drana Plantation.

This is the base of the Balaur army that protects Poeta Island.
Located high above, it keeps a close watch on all sides of Poeta.

A supply base that once stored and distributed combat provisions for the Ishtar Brigade during the Balaur's ancient war. It was particularly notorious for its mobile bombs, which inflicted massive Daeva casualties. Even now, long after the Balaur have occupied Eltnen, several of these mobile bombs remain deep within the base. Due to the passage of time, no one dares to salvage them out of fear that they may detonate unpredictably. Only the Balaur send occasional patrols to inspect the bombs and monitor the state of the base.
Built to honor a Daeva named Uruthum who led eleven warriors to slay the giant Drake Minusha during the Millennium War, this site has since crumbled to ruins.

One of the closest outposts to Kromede's Island.
The starting point for any travel throughout Iralcig Highland.
Kromede's followers tell time based on where the sun is relative to the Fire Temple.

A small base near the entrace to the Mystic Spring of Anathe.
It was once used for observation and recording the condition of the spring itself.
It was abandoned after the Lepharists occupied the Mystic Spring of Anathe.

A place in the shadow of the collapsed walls of the Verteron Fortress Ruins. 
A base once used as a hideout by some of the disbanded Illusion Cavaliers.

A village build on the Lacephin Mystic Spring, it fell into ruin when the Life Daeva scattered and the spring dried up. After a long period of abandonment, a Daeva named Chloris rebuilt and revived the village with her companions.
The village is able to survive in barren Eltnen due to its independent water supply.

A secret research base where the Balaur conduct biological experiments on Daeva.
Defeat the test subjects before they are fully transformed into Sura or mutated by Fafnite, and recover the remaining Odyle.

A high-ranking officer and confidant of Gerod, he played an active role in the founding of the Blades by providing financial support.

Like Gerod, he was born into a noble family of Asmodae. However, his cruel nature caused trouble from an early age, making him a burden and embarrassment to his family.

Deeply obsessed with the power of Fafnite, he willingly participates in Gerod's torment of Nemon.
A secret base built by the Dawn Legion in Verteron's Cantas Valley. It is hidden deep in the cliff and used as a hideout from the Balaur.

A bitterly cold lake, surrounded by thick mist. Its black waters are heavily polluted by runoff from the Gribade mines, making it difficult even to approach and earning it the moniker "the Lake of the Dead".

An exile colony home to legionnaires and Cavaliers who committed heinous crimes. Following the Balaur occupation of Verteron, it fell under Aullaeu control and now imprisons those banished from the Urugugu tribe.

A building that once housed Zikel's Faithful before they entered the sanctum, until a Balaur bombardment destroyed all but the basement. It now serves as a hideout for the Fang Legion as they fight against the Balaur.
The southern of two floating islands bearing the scars of a Dredgion crash.
A base for the Spirit Guides and Nornir that came to investigate the Sacred Tree Grisilla in relation to the strange happenings in the Purifying Forest.
A powerful impact split the floating island that once housed the fortress into two. This is the northern island.

An underwater cavern serves as the lair of Daine of Tears, the Water Spirit who once escaped from the cave where the Etheria Rift was formed.

Now severed from its pact-bearer, the spirit remains in a dangerously unstable state, its essence in constant turmoil.
Sulfur Tree Island - River of Rotten Sap
The border between the Tolbas Forest and the Aullaeu Village. It is the site of a war of nerves between the Shugo of Wind Breeze Merchants and the Urugugu tribe of Aullaeu.
Below the Dredgion Crash Site Cliff
This cave is where defeated Guardians hid from the Balaur and eventually met their ends. It holds the records of the Guardians of Verteron, who fought a fierce battle against the Ishtar Brigade.
A temporary home for the Draconute scouts who monitor the area around Drana Plantation.

An echo of Empyrean Lord Zikel, once the revered protector of Gladiators and Templars. He invoked the <QK>Blood Oath</> to bring down Dragon Lord Fafnir, though he himself was ultimately destroyed in the conflict.

After countless years sealed within the Impetusium, his lingering essence has faded into that of an Apparition.
In Front of Azrakar Brigade Prison Compound

A site that once housed records of research conducted by a Balaur named Iagosh and some humans. Today, all of those records have been destroyed or relocated, and the facility now serves as a temporary storage for all tribute collected from the Shugo.
The nest of the Mutant Valka, a giant insectoid that was mutated by contaminants leaking out from the crashed Dredgion.

An underground prison where those defeated in war were locked away. Over the years, the long-forgotten Prison of Oblivion has become filled only with restless dead and swarming rats, but rumors whisper of a lost chronicle hidden deep within its walls.

An ancient Morheim temple, where Kromede found herself imprisoned while searching for treasure.
The impact of AION's fragments falling upon Morheim allowed Kromede's fragmented self, split by the Mirror of Illusion, to escape.
A <QK>southern camp</> base located in the south of Chaotic Upper Reshanta.

A sanctum filled with endless resentment and blood-stained loathing.
You must destroy the minions who feed on hatred together with their master, and conquer the cursed power.
The Scribe's Room is believed that it was part of the Zumion Temple. The scribe left behind many records, but those on paper have been weathered away by time, and only a few stone tablets remain.
Moslan Forest bandits have made a hideout out of an old prison for Asmodian Daeva.

A temporary outpost once used by the Dawn Legion.
It is currently abandoned and no longer in use.

Located close to the Executioner's Tower, frequent clashes between the Fate Archons and Kromede's followers occur here.
Kromede has used the base to maintain balance between the forces, seeing how highly the Archons seem to value the Executioner's Tower.
A hidden cave rich in rare minerals. Crystalline monsters are swarming within.

A small and unassuming campsite built on the highland by clerics trying to clean up Meslamtaeda's poison blood. It is said that some of the surviving priests of Zumion once sealed the poison in a sacred well to prevent it from spreading, knowing it would rot the land if left untreated.
The middle stretches of the Ellun River, which flows through Verteron. It has a relatively clean environment.
A cave that is home to the Giant Karnif Istan—a ferocious beast that emerged as the apex predator in a bitter, cold land without Mau. Strangely enough, it shares a nest with a Debry.
Destroy Unstable Odylium to obtain Odyle Orbs.
A floating island formed by the merger of part of Sulfur Tree Island.

<QK>Kromede's ego</>, split by the mirror.
She mustered all her strength to find the Artifact in the hopes of saving her lover, Robstin, but the Artifact she found had no such power.
With all her hopes shattered, she returned to the mirror in frustration, eventually deteriorating to her current state of being, consumed by rage and desire.

A Karas den located in northern Morheim. Originally a hideout for a small group of Nornir, it was eventually raided by the Balaur. Most of its inhabitants were either murdered for resisting or processed as materials for Fafnite, leaving behind a cursed legacy that deters anyone from approaching the area.
A temporary camp set up by Creion for researching the Dredgion.

A den of the Ferocious Horn Mau tribe, located in the Abyss.
Through constant use of Fafnite, the Ferocious Horn Mau managed to survive within the Abyss, but many lives were lost on the way.
After fully embracing the power of Fafnite, the Ferocious Horn tribe is now pioneering a new life in the Abyss while keeping the memory of the fallen alive.
A small clearing between the stones and fallen trees. The young Elim used to come here and play, but the Blood Blades set it ablaze and destroyed it.

A wide plain in the heart of Eltnen. Only traces remain of the village and forest that stood on this once-fertile land.
It links together the rocky highlands of the Fractured Land and the wastes of the Eracus Desert.

An underground Lepharist laboratory.
A giant explosion from a failed experiment destroyed the laboratory.
Access was later restored through the culvert, but it currently lies unused.
An outpost garrisoned by Balaur of the Lagta Brigade. Responsible for hunting down any local resistance, they are notorious for being among the most brutal of the Balaur.

An artificial hatchery where Balaur use dead Dramata to make Dratona.
Decomposing even as it still draws breath, and consumed by twisted obsessions, the Dramata Durvati nests in and guards the hatchery.
A cave on the side of a dumpsite for organic waste derived from Drana cultivation. It is also used as a hideout by the Salvation Legion before they escape after rescuing their imprisoned comrades.

The base of the Ratcatchers, a group that kidnaps refugees in Lacephin Village and trades them for profit. Named after their tendency to refer to victims as 'rats', its members infamously revel in the criminality of their actions.

A Garzykan fort located in the southeast of Chaotic Middle Reshanta.

In the aftermath of the Last War, the space comprising Reshanta began to warp, causing a number of the floating islands that had been part of the Ancient City of Ru—located on the upper layer of Reshanta—to be sucked downward by the gravitational pull of the Latesran Roots, until they formed a new, middle layer.

This displacement largely destroyed Garzykan Fortress, and it now comprises three floating islands connected by bridges with a massive wall encircling their outer perimeter.

A brutal training ground where Mumu Laborers are forged into warriors through relentless discipline. Those who fail to endure the overseer’s harsh regimen are cast into the depths of the prison’s grasp.

Following the molten lava that flows deep within the cave leads directly into the heart of the Fire Temple. The spirits here, bound to the structure's power, became twisted and corrupted the very day Kromede abandoned the temple.

A temporary campsite located in Eastern Cantas Valley.
A place where passing Daeva and merchants stay temporarily.

A cave that now stands as a tomb to pilgrims who succumbed to Sura mutation. Their fellow Illusion God pilgrims continue to pray inside, wishing them peaceful slumber, but the Sura—whose grudges run deep—may awaken again at any moment.
A hidden refuge where Reckless Jonas, who fled the Blades to escape punishment, now hides alongside his followers. It was once a sanctuary where ascetics trained in solitude.
This is a settlement of the Urugugu tribe, an Aullaeu people who followed Tiamat and migrated from the Dragon World. Now they worship Ishtar instead of Tiamat.
Hideout in Front of the Ruins
