A burial vault beneath Verteron Fortress. It likely contains a great number of Daeva relics, with its underground location having allowed it to escape Balaur bombardment.
A campsite for thieves trading in suspicious herbs looted from nearby farms, with a foul smell hanging in the air and frequent unsavory visitors.
A small base naturally formed around a waterfall as more and more people move in and out of the area. Refugees, grave robbers and relic seekers travelling to and from the Basfelt Ruins.

A cave rumored to be haunted by the souls of Elyos unable to return to Elysea. Stories say that the Elyos here were trapped in Asmodae while investigating the Abyss alongside Deltras, the Guardian of Elysium.
An outpost located on a cliff outside the Dawn Legion Base. It overlooks eastern Cantas.
A Balaur Prison Compound located along the Kraka Footpath. Due to its environment being well-suited for incubation of Dratona, it is currently used as a temporary hatching ground.

A Drakan member of Meslamtaeda's Seker Strike Force who operates alone to spy on and sabotage Daeva, using power inherited from Meslamtaeda to hide himself away in realms of his own creation. Normal Daeva cannot detect him, but those blessed with "Daeva Sense" may use it to uncover his tracks.

Lauded for his discipline, patience, and intelligence, he is entrusted with spying on the most important Daeva bases. Though he has been ordered to focus on spying rather than killing, he often craves Daeva blood, and will deliberately leave tracks behind in the hope of luring new prey.

A Balaur surveillance base built to aid the search for the Ascension Artifact. Functionally a forward base, it collects intel from the fake Fate Archons and reports any findings to the Fafnir Brigade's main forces. The base is littered with Fafnium, which is used to trap the souls of Daeva captured by the fake Fate Archons. Much of the victims tend to be Kromede's followers.
The place where Zikel and the Destruction Archons fought against Dragon Lord Fafnir until the bitter end. Nobody can enter because of the barrier formed by Zikel's spilled blood.
The Drana Depository of the Balaur, guarded by the Depository Manager Arya, infamous for his brutal slaying of Daeva.
There are Daeva who, despite not being Sura, have strayed from the Daeva path and sworn to serve the Balaur. This cave is the home to such Daeva Renegades.
A small campsite inhabited by the Illusion Cavaliers.

Inherently inquisitive, the Creion are famed for seeking out dangerous places to conduct dangerous experiments. This cave is one of many such places, abandoned following an experiment that ended in failure. However, perhaps they left some valuable items behind.

An abandoned cave where a Daeva who betrayed the Blades was imprisoned, tortured, and left to die. It is said that the restless spirit of the traitor, along with the vengeful souls of other slain Daeva, haunts the cave and attacks all who dare enter.

A place where the memories of the vanished Elyos Empyrean Lord <QK>Zikel</> remain as fragments of dreams. Though little more than a dream, the Empyrean Lord's power over destruction remains vibrant, and he has no mercy for the Elyos he detests so much.

A prison operated by the Balaur in the Dranactus region, used to imprison Daeva who oppose the Balaur, and torture them for information that will help them eradicate the local Legions. Captured Daeva are forced into labor, and turned into Fafnite when they are of no use.
A small hall at the bottom of Impetusium Hill. It once housed a statue of Daeva, the winners of the Impetusium, but now it has been destroyed and only traces remain.

A sanctum in the Verteron Fortress Ruins. When Verteron Fortress was invaded, the Illusion Cavaliers took their artifacts and made their last stand in this place. In order to defend the sanctum, the Illusion Cavaliers set up various defenses inside.

Krall are assigned by the Balaur to handle the disposal of the large amounts of waste produced by experiments conducted in Nahid Brigade Fortress, and of the byproducts produced by the nearby Drana Plantation. The number of Krall specialized in these tasks is substantial enough to require an entire barracks.
A military base of the Balaur, garrisoned by Fafnir's Azrakar Brigade.
An eastern camp base located in the northeast of Chaotic Lower Reshanta.
Rubek Thieves' Occupied Territory Treasure Storage

A library created in Moslan Forest by Musein, a librarian who sought to preserve the knowledge of the Asmodians by creating a secret library. Whispers tell of ancient tomes on the Bulwark kept within this library's depths.

A place overrun by mutants contaminated by Fafnite, where the supplies of Shulak merchants who were mining Fafnite Gemstone still remain untouched.
It is likely you can recover many of these lost supplies, as well as a number of treasures held by the mutants.
Originally a rest stop for visitors to the forest, the Elim came to stay here when visitors came less frequently. There are no Elim left after the Blades set fire to it.
The northernmost region of Chaotic Middle Reshanta. The broken remains of giant mechanical soldiers used in the Last War lie abandoned here.
A facility where Dragon Lord Fafnir manufactures Fafnite using Fafnium containing stolen souls, and conducts various experiments with human and Daeva Fafnite.
A plateau in the highland and canyon region of eastern Verteron, including the former site of Zumion Temple and the area contaminated by the poison of Meslamtaeda.

A fortress built by Dragon Lord Ishtar when he conquered Poeta Island.
Inside, there are numerous test tubes at work turning Daeva into Sura while Ishtar's army stands guard.

Once a small legion that resisted the Balaur, after a particularly brutal defeat, they decided instead to use illusion magic known as the Eye of Enchantment to abduct villagers in pursuit of expanding their influence.
An ancient cave once used by the Lepharists to conduct experiments on Krao. Though long abandoned, it is said that the surviving test subjects still roam its shadowy depths.

A small cavern tucked away on the outskirts of the Ruberein Hills. While it appears completely ordinary from the outside, there are whispers of an endless spring of pristine water deep within. Rumor has it that the source of this pure water is an ancient relic left behind by the Life Daeva, hidden far beneath the spring's depths.
Drawn by these tales, bandits from across the region flock to the cave.
A cave where a passage to the Abyss has appeared. It contains information about the Ancient City of Ru.

The interior of the Sacred Tree Grisilla.
During the war, the Balaur drilled a hole into the Sacred Tree that protected the forest, with the goal of destroying it.
Daeva ventured inside, hoping to stop the Balaur, only to be defeated following a brutal battle.
The Poison Blood left behind by the Dragon Lord clings to the roots of Grisilla, contaminating them deeply and driving the Spirits of the forest to madness.

A land littered with ruined tombs and ancient relics, now overrun by wraiths and other undead.
Though abandoned, this land untouched by time boasts buried riches and long-forgotten resources.

A place where the Balaur dispose of contaminants and living beings used in their experiments, namely Daeva.
As immortal demigods, Daeva are not easily destroyed, no matter how brutally they are experimented upon.
Instead of looking for ways to dispose of Daeva who have exhausted their usefulness, the Balaur decided simply to abandon them to die on their own.
As such, the Chimera Dumpsite has accumulated two centuries worth of discarded experimental subjects, becoming a hellish place filled with contaminants and creatures driven purely by violent instinct, no longer recognizable as the Daeva they once were.

Reshanta, located in the Abyss—the subspace created from the unstable energies of the split AION Tower—has long been a battlefield where the Elyos, Asmodian, and Balaur clash.
Access to Reshanta had been forbidden for a time due to the Odyle storm unleashed by the collapse of AION over 200 years ago, but a century later, Daeva were once again allowed to enter it.

But now, Reshanta has turned into a realm that is twisted beyond recognition by the aftermath of the collapse. The world beyond the base shifted unpredictably, sometimes even linking to the same faction in entirely different dimensions. The Daeva fell into anguish and confusion when they were forced to confront others who bore wings of the same color as their own.

Yet, they could not halt their advance. Unlike Elysea and Asmodae, where Odyle has been dwindling, Reshanta still brimmed with abundant Odyle left behind by the storm. They face a grim fate now, and to survive, they must raise their blades even against their own kind.

[Temporary text for testing] The western region of Cantas Valley. The area is largely unremarkable, but occasionally lucky adventurers can witness Void flying across the sky on a clear day. According to tales passed down among Daeva, this great humpback whale of the sky carries the bravest of the brave on its back to the Eternal Isle.

The former Chief Guardian of the Aullaeu Altar.

Aulak resisted Reda’s mind-control magic for a time, but eventually succumbed, causing both his body and mind to become twisted by its influence. Once a proud guardian of the Aullaeu, he has since been reduced to a hunched and featherless creature, stripped of his former dignity. Yet even in his corrupted state, his claws remain more deadly than ever.

<QK>Pino</>, a towering wooden doll brought to life through Aullaeu sorcery to serve as the altar's guardian. A shamanic emblem of the Aullaeu is carved into the center of its chest, marking its sacred purpose.
A den imprisoning Razekin, a Shulak who survived Fafnite dust poisoning, but at the cost of his sanity.
A hilly area between the Nameless Cemetery and the Sanctum Outpost.

A vault containing the riches of the Barrier Tower Fortress. Concentrated fire from the Balaur has reduced its entrance to rubble, giving it the unassuming appearance of a cave. The valuables within are still intact, though guarded by the wraiths of Daeva who fell during the attack.
It is the grave of an unknown reader who never let go of a book until the moment of the death. There may have been some rare books in the reader's collection.

A fortress in the Abyss established by Ludra of the Tempest, who was defeated by Daeva in the past before being revived through the power of the abyss.
Utilizing that same power, Ludra has been transforming his followers into a mighty army and relentlessly reshaping himself as he dreams of bringing Atreia to its knees with his new, Abyss-forged legion.
When the Aullaeu crossed over to the Verteron, they worshipped the new Dragon Lord Ishtar as their god at ceremonial sites like this.
A base for the Spirit Guides who are investigating the strange phenomena happening in the Purifying Forest.

A cavern occupied by the outlaws of the Patamor Plains. Composed primarily of former Blades members, this gang has risen to infamy by robbing travelers and merchants journeying between Altgard and Morheim.
A cave claimed as a base by a Draconute warband led by Lamnah, the ruthless Scouts Captain of the Lagta Brigade.

This place was Poeta Island's very own Forest of Elim, until the Balaur conquered the island and the Elim disappeared. Few traces of them now remain, and it is now only remembered s a place where countless Daeva once achieved their ascension.
A cave containing abnormal amounts of Fungie. Rumor says that treasure lies deep within, but none have successfully ventured far enough inside.
You can earn a large amount of Kina.

An outpost established by Blades in Moslan Forest to facilitate hunting down any surviving Nornir. Rumor has it that somewhere within the outpost lies a treasure chest filled with valuables looted from the Nornir.

A valley where Daeva who resisted the Balaur invasion once sought refuge, only to find it become their final resting place after a Dredgion bombardment. Many of those who fought here had served since the days before the Balaur invasion.

The collapse of AION Tower tore dimensions asunder, and it was into one such tear that Legion Commander Bakarma was drawn. Enduring an almost infinite span of time within Draupnir, a subspace that has absorbed the energy of countless other dimensions, he, too, accumulated immense power. Now broken free from the bonds of his physical form, Bakarma has become a transcendent being, agonizing over how to reshape the universe in his image.

The former High Priestess of Kaisinel and leader of the Illusion Cavaliers, Reda was a Spiritmaster of extraordinary power and a favored servant of Empyrean Lord Kaisinel. She chose to remain beyond the Bulwark, dedicating herself to the sacred duty of protecting the Core of the Illusion God.

Reda’s unwavering devotion to safeguarding the Core and her daughter sustained her through countless years of hardship. Yet this same resolve drew the resentment of others, who condemned her for abandoning the Illusion Cavaliers to their tragic fate.

When her daughter was ultimately slain by the Balaur, and Phernos failed to return despite his promise, the weight of loss became unbearable. Consumed by grief and hatred, Reda was slowly transformed by the very despair she had fought so long to endure.

A forest protected by the power of the ancient Sacred Tree Grisilla. Because of the contamination resulting from Fafnir's Poison Blood, Grisilla has weakened and the entire forest is losing its purifying powers.
Rumors whisper of treasure hidden in this abandoned Odylium mine, but all who have ventured inside fell victim to swarms of Odyle Spiders.

A spring that was abandoned following the Balaur Invasion. Treasures moved here during its construction still remain. However, the area is highly dangerous, as Slimes contaminated by the Mystic Spring of Anathe roam the area.

Spirit Flowers have been known to grow in some hidden caves along the middle reaches of the Ellun River. Once common, they have become increasingly rare due to pollution and indiscriminate illegal harvesting for use as a medicinal herb or ingredients for magic. A number of groups have occupied the caves and are indiscriminately harvesting Spirit Flowers illegally.

A Sura who manages the Disposal Plant at Nahid Fortress.

Modified for combat specialization, it possesses formidable combat abilities but retains none of the memories, personality, or even appearance it had during its time as a Daeva. It was once deployed as a soldier to protect Ishtar Castle, but after the Dawn Legion's attack on Poeta, it was demoted and assigned to the Disposal Plant.

It finds Daeva who attempt to steal from the facility to be especially annoying.
One of the storages used by the Blades when they were mainly operating in Morheim. Gerod is said to have frequented the repository despite the area's steep terrain.

Originally a plain old cave in the Nameless Cemetery, it later became a place where Karas were trapped and killed.
Rumor has it that those who were buried alive are still haunting the cave even after death. Unsurprisingly, none have dared approach to confirm this.

The Beritra Brigade persist in building their flying fortresses in various places, eyes set on Atreia.
Defeat their high commander and annihilate their forces.

It is not uncommon for those undergoing Sura mutation to deny reality and seek to return to their original forms by curing their symptoms, hiding away as they conduct research through often unethical methods.
A cave used by Aullaeu Shamans for their ritual studies, guarded by Konutins stationed in the area.
A large river that bisects the eastern region of Altgard from north to south. After the fall of AION, the river basin expanded because of changes to the landscape.

An old sanctum where the priests of the Zumion Temple held meetings and prayed until it was destroyed by Meslamtaeda, leaving only a few stepping stones and pillars. Following Meslamtaeda's invasion, the surviving priests sealed Meslamtaeda's Poison Blood in the Purifying Altar, but the seal has since broken, resulting in a dangerous place filled with leaking poison and rampaging Guardite.
Archipelago of Siel's Wings - Grave of Steel
Together with Spiritmasters, the Dawn Legion has established a base to facilitate the restoration of the Verteron Barrier Tower after it was shattered in an attack by the Ishtar Brigade.
A cave where Daeva fleeing the Balaur hid while gathering their strength for a counterattack.
A base occupied mainly by gravekeepers.

Once a sacred temple imbued with Yustiel's blessings and the very essence of life, a dimensional rift caused it to become submerged in an unknown place, where it was transformed into an underwater dimension where light and even time are distorted.
As a result, the resident Daeva had their own life essence warped, twisting their physical forms beyond recognition. They now retain only the instinct to protect their temple.

A base by the Eltnen Barrier Tower Ruins belonging to Chloris's band.
Used as a site for searching the ruins for the Artifact.
One of Yustiel's Lifestone relics remains here.

A spring near Muspel Volcano, located under a cliff so dangerous that not even the treasure hunter Kromede has dared to get close—or at least, according to the rumors. Many a starry-eyed explorer has ventured here in hopes of surpassing Kromede's glory.
A former outpost of the Daeva warriors who fought to defend Zumion Temple, long destroyed and reduced to its framework. There are a few Notos Legionnaires and Revenants still retaining some sanity.

The western region of the Cantas Valley. Since Odylium was discovered here and a number of collectors were installed, it has long served as a key source of Odylium for the Daeva for some time. The Dawn Legion has repaired the collectors and is gathering the scarce Odyle.

The Creion of Eltnen used their advanced technology to combat the desertification of the region and repel the invading Balaur. However, as Eltnen was never historically a stronghold for their race, their individual efforts quickly hit a wall, forcing most Creion to abandon the wasteland. Yet, a researcher named Malgerre refused to leave, determined to perfect a way to save Eltnen. Continuing his work alone in a small cave, Malgerre’s obsession eventually drove him to use his own body as a test subject. Tragically, the experiment ended in catastrophic failure, mutating him into a hideous monster.

An outpost garrisoned by low-level Balaur troops, serving as a watchtower over the Ellun River Midstream and Verteron Fortress Ruins. Any Shugo or Daeva seen passing by will likely be attacked solely for entertainment.

A <QK>candidate for Arch Daeva</> born after the Last War and <QK>leader of the Lepharists</> in Elysea.
He rose to his current position by helping with Dragon Lord Ishtar's Sura research, seeming to be minion of the Balaur, but was actually cultivating his own power.
He is arrogant because of his genius, and has rejected Asahr's revelations as enslavement by AION.
His ultimate goal is to become a <QK>god</> greater than the Balaur, Daeva, and even AION.

A woman buried alive within an Altgard crypt, who returned as a Karas. Once an ordinary girl, she was unjustly sacrificed and sealed away without reason. Even in undeath, she could not forget the profound hatred born from that betrayal.

The tune she once hummed in her final moments has long since twisted into something else, now escaping her only as mournful wails and broken sobs.
A jail situated under the Verteron Fortress. Though currently under Krall control, it still contains many relics and writings of Illusion Cavaliers.
A forest where fireflies, mysterious natural vegetation, and Tunapre Lake come together.
Zikel's zealots grow their power within these underground caves. Corrupted followers blindly worship the kept records of Zikel, spreading false faith throughout Altgard.
A stronghold once used by the Dawn Legion to assist in restoring the Barrier Tower in the Ellun River Marsh. It is no longer used after relations with the Illusion Cavaliers deteriorated.
Archipelago of Siel's Wings - Siel's Heart
A hiding place of Daeva who have strayed from the Daeva path and now serve the Balaur.
A base located near the Dredgion ship that crashed in the Calderon Canyon. Access to Dredgion is impossible due to the Drakana oozing out of the ship.
A Notos Legion base located near the entrance of the Scarlet Forest. It was established to observe the activity within the Scarlet Forest.
A base belonging to the notorious criminal Kius and his followers. The bounty on his head from the Notos Legion has grown higher and higher, but no one has dared attempt to capture him.
A spring imbued with restorative powers that can clear an area of any toxic aura. Since the Purifying Forest has been losing its power, the spring's power has also been weakening.

Traces within the cave suggest that until relatively recently it was being used as a shelter for Life Daeva who scattered following the disappearance of Yustiel.
Thanks to the direct intervention of these Life Daeva with purification devices, the water within the cave remains remarkably pure, a rarity in the rapidly desertifying region of Eltnen. However, following the departure of the Life Daeva, these same devices have started failing due to lack of maintenance, and it is uncertain when the water might cease flowing.

The base of Kromede, the treasure hunter who once shook up all of Asmodae.
The only one who knows how she was able to acquire a place like this is Kromede herself.
Despite the harsh conditions, just a quick look around shows that her followers are happy to have been brought here by Kromede herself.

Karas fled the village to this cave, but their fate could not be avoided. Though sealed in the past, the ravages of time have once again reopened this Karas-infested den. They continue to lurk within, mad and hungry for prey.

A graveyard for those who died fighting the Balaur. The sheer amount of dead has meant that many were buried without headstones, and the spirits of those Daeva who failed to return to the flow of Odyle roam freely.
During the fall of Verteron Fortress, this hideout was a garrison of the Illusion Cavalier Spiritmasters guarding the fortress. They fought fiercely against the Balaur, but were eventually wiped out.

Once serving as a place of worship to Yustiel, this Life Temple has since fallen under the control of the Lepharists.
Following the fall of a dazzlingly bright light nearby several years ago, it has also earned the name of Light Crash Site.

A temporary camp built by the Dawn Legion on the coastal side of Cantas Valley. Dawn legionnaires searching for the Odyle in Cantas Valley built this camp to facilitate investigating the coastal cave.

Draupnir Cave is a stronghold built in Bellusran by the Bakarma Brigade. After the collapse of the AION Tower, Draupnir Cave was swept away in the chaos of Atreia and fell into the Abyss.
While wandering the Abyss, Bakarma discovered a power that did not exist in Atreia and sought to use it to become a being transcending the Balaur.
A cave known to grow rare herbs. However, the animals that ate the herbs grew too strong, and the cave became inaccessible to humans.

The Blades' former base from when they were still active in Morheim. As remote as it is barren, it was the perfect location for them to continue their activities without alerting the residents of Patamor Village or Kromede's followers.

A root cavity created by the deep roots of a large and old tree in the Tolbas Forest.
It once served as an assembly hall and chapel for Aullaeu Village. Now it is used to store food, weapons, and ceremonial items for the whole tribe.
The ground of the ruins of the Altamia Highland. The Zumion Temple and its surroundings, submerged by extreme weather after the Last War, have risen to the surface.
A new base for the Nornir, who have gathered here from all over Moslan Forest while fleeing the attacks of the Blood Blades. The residence of Urd, who leads the Nornir, is here.

A forest near the Drana Plantation and Nahid Brigade Fortress, with vegetation turned red by the influence of Drana. Escaped Sura and Daeva Wraiths roam between the trees, and Balaur scouts are on regular patrols.

Some of the Shulak criminals who roamed the Abyss continued their criminal activities even after settling in Altgard. In particular, a smuggler named Sumakhi will stop at nothing to make a profit and is now notorious among Daeva and humans for his brutality.

Once a sanctum under the administration of the High Priestess of Illusion, it has since been neglected and turned to ruins.
While waiting in vain for their Empyrean Lord's return, the priests were captured by the Balaur and turned into Sura, who now attack anyone who enters the sanctum.
This is where the stone statue of Uruthum was erected to share the news of triumph after defeating the great Drake Minusha.

A Garzykan fort located in the northwest of Chaotic Middle Reshanta.

In the aftermath of the Last War, the space comprising Reshanta began to warp, causing a number of the floating islands that had been part of the Ancient City of Ru—located on the upper layer of Reshanta—to be sucked downward by the gravitational pull of the Latesran Roots, until they formed a new, middle layer.

This displacement largely destroyed Garzykan Observatory, and it now comprises three floating islands connected by bridges with a massive wall encircling their outer perimeter.

The hiding place of Dehinon, who is both Daeva and non-Daeva. Kidnapped and taken to the Nahid Brigade's base, he managed to escape in the process of being turned into a Sura. Hiding in this cave with his comrades, he is slowly losing his sanity.
A secret library built in Basfelt by Musein, a librarian who sought to preserve the knowledge of the Asmodians. Whispers tell of ancient tomes containing information on the Bulwark.

A cave serving as the hiding place of Deios, a corrupted Spiritmaster who was one of many who lost their way following Kaisinel's extinction and the dissolution of the Illusion Cavaliers. Out of sight of other Daeva, Deios has been researching dangerous magic in hopes of finding a way to control the spirits of Etheria.

Once the main base of the Destruction Archons operating near Zikel's Sanctum, it has since been taken over by the Balaur. Now that the Daeva's rebellion has been quelled, Draconute troops manage the area.
Destroy the Giant Fafnium and defeat the boss.

Sura are Daeva who mutated after having all of their life energy drained by the Balaur. A number of Sura secluded themselves in caves while they still retained their sanity, attempting to halt their mutation. Ultimately, however, all succumbed to their fate of becoming mindless monsters.

The majority of refugees in Eltnen have gathered and live in the Refugee Camp on Eiron Hill.
Most Eiron Hill refugees are peaceful and law-abiding, maintaining good relations with the Tsenka Merchants and Chloris.
Drok and his band of outlaws are an outlier. By inciting disgruntled refugees to desert their camp, Drok has established a base for him and his group. Now operating as marauders, they survive on scraps of the chaos left behind by the Hilsrother Marauders and Lepharists.

A cave where pilgrims worshipping the Illusion God practiced meditation. The High Priestess of Illusion summoned Spirits to guard this place for the pilgrims, but after strange things began happening in the garden following her disappearance, pilgrims gradually stopped coming.
Now, only the Spirits remain, guarding an empty cave.
The highlands located between the Western and Eastern Gribade Highlands, to the south of Idun's Lake. The road to Zemurru's Tomb is located here, but it is not being maintained.

A cave inhabited by Biruta—unique creatures found in Tolbas Forest and prized by the Shugo for the special properties of their leaves. The gentle-natured Biruta live quietly in small family groups throughout the cave.

A place where the Fafnium used throughout the Sanctum Outpost is managed by the Lagta Brigade. The Lagta Brigade has been using Fafnium created by Dragon Lord Fafnir to steal the souls of countless Daeva and control their empty flesh. This place is being guarded by Sentinel Nuraka of the Lagta Brigade.

One of the many hidden Lepharist research centers spread across Eltnen.
The facility is home to a myriad of research initiatives—including processing Drana into energy and breeding test subjects.
However, its test subject research has been halted for reasons unknown.

A shrine to Illusion God Kaisinel, built by his own order before the Second Great Catastrophe.
Ardus Shrine and its surroundings were crystallized by energy from the Spirit Realm and the power of Kaisinel, and now glows with a blackish-purple light much like Kaisinel's own brilliance. The surrounding vegetation absorbs the energy to grow lush, and glows too at night.

A hilly area along the middle stretches of Ellun River. Daeva who scattered across Verteron following various defeats against the Balaur rallied together, seeking a chance to strike back. Ultimately, they perished without ever even crossing these hills.
A cellar beneath the tree housing Kumrica, a member of the Daybreak Society. Inside are food, weapons, and other supplies needed for survival in an emergency.

The ruins of a temple on a sky island, brought down by a direct strike from a Balaur Dredgion. It has since become the lair of renegade Daeva, who extort and murder any other Daeva who cross their path.

After the fall of AION, a section of the of the Arcanis Air Temple fell into the Abyss and was tainted by the power of the Void. In the process, beings of the Void absorbed the temple's spirits and were reborn with new bodies, and now occupy the shattered temple.
A valley formed when Kuriullu Crag was split by tectonic activity.
A base used to assist in transporting goods from the Drana Plantation to the Nahid Brigade Fortress.

A magical knight that guards the <QK>Illusion Sanctum</> where Kaisinel concealed forbidden knowledge.

Usually dormant in the form of ornamental armor, it awakens the moment an intruder enters the sanctum and does not rest until the threat has been eliminated.

The purple glow that emanates from its body is a result of residual traces of Scarlotus, left behind when it was cast within the Illusion Sanctum.

The hideout of Selmar and his fellow Daeva, who are driven by delusions to mercilessly attack innocent Daeva. They believe themselves to be the only true Daeva, and all Daeva who pass through to be their enemies.
The entrance to a subterranean cave system flooded with groundwater. Rumors speak of treasure awaiting in the depths of the cave, drawing the attention of fortune seekers time and time again.

One of the outposts built by Patamor Village residents to keep an eye on the Balaur in the plains.
It can also serve as a signal post to evacuate villagers in the event of danger.

A place where refugees have stayed after a giant object fell out of the sky and destroyed their homes in the village on the hill.
Some refugees moved to Lacephin Village to escape the hardship, but some former scholars have been unable to leave due to their research on the ruins on Eiron Hill.
You can earn a large amount of Kina.
A den of the Akilo Thieves who have become somewhat notorious in the Ellun River Midstream.

The departure point for Kromede's followers traveling to Nephra Snowfield or Patamor Village.
Unlike the volcanic zone, this also serves as a checkpoint because of the bridge leading to Kromede's Island.
A peaceful hill on the outskirts of the Sanctum Outpost.
An <QK>eastern camp</> base located in the east of Chaotic Middle Reshanta.

A Spirit of Etheria who serves the Spirit King.

After Kaisinel and Lumiel were destroyed, the Spirit King deemed all contracts with Daeva to have ended. He now seeks to bring every spirit under his direct control. Gartua has begun recalling to Etheria any spirits who traveled to Atreia without permission, while forcing others to sever their contracts with Spiritmasters.

Gartua can freely traverse the Rift, the space between Atreia and Etheria, allowing him to manipulate and exert his influence over the fabric of space itself.
A small stretch of land connecting northern and southern Altgard. Once a crucial trading hub for Shulak merchants, it now serves as little more than a bridge.
A marauder hideout hidden within the Purifying Forest. This group particularly despises the Karas and loots all forest inhabitants, Nornirs and Karas alike.

A group that hunts indiscriminately in Tolbas Forest. They do not hesitate to attack other humans or Shugo. Recently, they are trying to cultivate Hallucinogenic Mushrooms, a rare and dangerous plant.

This place was once a village of loggers and hunters until it was largely destroyed by the Balaur. Now it is overgrown bush, and the terrain where the Balaur bombardment was concentrated is pitted and twisted, leaving only the shattered ruins of Zikel's Temple.
A makeshift base set up by the Daeva dispatched to the Dredgion crash site in Calderon Canyon.

The terrain surrounding Kromede's Island, located between the sheer cliffs of the snowfield and roiling volcanic lava.
The coast spreads out wide at the land's end, but the land itself is empty and covered with ash.
The elevated areas of the western highlands and canyon region surrounding Zumion Village. Includes the former site of Zumion Temple and the area contaminated by the poison of Meslamtaeda.

Following Kaisinel's disappearance, contracts with the spirits were broken and Etheria grew increasingly unstable, resulting in many spirits turning violent. This cave is one such place overrun with unruly spirits.
The ruins of a destroyed sanctum, said to contain records written by Empyrean Lord Zikel.

One of the mysterious caves containing fragments that fell all over Atreia when AION collapsed.
From the Dream Remnants, you must retrieve the <QK>Fragment of Will</>, which contains the pain and memories of AION.
The <QK>Fragment of Will</> is under the protection of the Dream Guardians.

The battle at the Nahid Brigade Fortress ended in total defeat for the Daeva. Many were captured or succumbed to extinction, and what few survived went into hiding in places such as the Cave of the Defeated.

A lair of criminals exiled from Safe Haven now ruled by Korhe, the deceiver who once shattered the village from within through cunning and betrayal. Rumor has it the hideout is overflowing with stolen riches, plundered artifacts, and other spoils taken in the chaos of the village's downfall.
A rest stop for Kuru working under the Aullaeu, where they can often be seen lounging around after a hard day's work.

A hill in the Altamia Highland filled with giant rocks that stand like gravestones. Originally a peaceful place, but after the war and Balaur invasion, this hill became a refuge for Daeva subjected to Balaur experiments. They soon turned into egoless Sura and now wander the hill aimlessly. Later on, with Renegade Daeva also finding refuge here, Rock Tomb Hill has earned a notorious reputation as a dangerous, lawless area.

An illusionary specter of Empyrean Lord Kaisinel, created from a fragment of his essence left behind before his destruction.

Though only a remnant of the original Kaisinel, it retains fragments of his memories and personality, including his arrogance and irritable nature. When the Bulwark was raised, Kaisinel was destroyed, yet traces of his presence endured within the sanctum, continuing to influence the surrounding area.
This ruin houses ancient Daeva chronicles, but it has since been claimed by exiled Mau who abandoned their oaths and made it their own.

A farm where the Wind Breeze Merchants raise livestock. The grasses of the Tolbas Forest provide good food for the livestock, but they are often attacked by Aullaeu and wild beasts, so a vigilante group has been formed. However, all of the members are inexperienced in combat.
The place where the soul-shattered cadets of Destruction Archons, slain for defying Hystan's command, are imprisoned in eternal despair
A small cave on the outskirts of Moslan Forest. It was used as a refuge by local residents when the forest was burning.
A Safe Haven Inspection Area managed by the village militia. It is used to defend against the invasion of the Legion Outlaws and to prevent unauthorized people from entering the village.

A volcanic zone created by unstable tectonic activity after the volcano in Muspel erupted, and location of the Fire Temple.
Equally as harsh as terrain as Nephra Snowfield for Kromede's followers.
Endless streams of lava flow out of Halabana Canyon.

A sanctum built by order of Kaisinel, Spiritmaster and God of Illusion. It was once a beautiful garden where spirits and fairies were bornbut after years left untended during the long war and Kaisinel's disappearance, it became a dangerous place where powerful spirits raged uncontrollably.

A secret depository of Crobakhi, the Shulak who earned a fortune by any means necessary.
He is said to have enjoyed swimming in towers of coins and hidden his vast wealth throughout Atreia.
A grassland located between the Eastern Cantas Valley and the Ellun River Marsh. The area still remains unpolluted and pristine.
An outpost built by the Notos Legion after Sura and Karas were witnessed near Zumion Village to ensure no threats come too close.

A mysterious place to the east of the Contaminated Marsh. The Spirit Tree has kept the surrounding area unpolluted with its pure power of Etheria. However, with the opening of the Etheria Rift and the disappearance of the spirit within the tree, it is once again under threat.

The lunatic researcher Sellutey intends to create a new world order by combining Lepharist technology with sorcery.
However, his rogue methods made him unpopular among his fellow Lepharists. Eventually, he came to occupy these ancient ruins, where he continues to focus on his life's work.

A dimensional rift created by the disruption of the boundary between Atreia and Etheria.
Etheria, the realm of the Spirits, was separated from Atreia by a contract between the Empyrean Lords and the Spirit Kings. However, when Kaisinel and Lumiel disappeared and the contract with the Spirits grew weak, rifts leading to Etheria began to appear across Atreia, and the rampaging Spirit King attempted to expand the spread of the rifts as well as his control over all of Atreia's Spirits.
A rest area for hunters. They hunt the nearby beasts and animals to make a living. Some hunters also trade fresh beast bones and skins here.

A mysterious rift said to lead to the Ancient City of Ru, known only to seasoned explorers.

Rumors claim that the lost records of Ru lie hidden deep within this cave.

An outpost briefly used by the Dawn Legion in the past.
It is currently abandoned and no longer in use.
A rest area for Shulak who guard the Gates of Fafnir.

An island that has grown uninhabitable after being polluted by waste from Nahid Fortress. Krao minerals grow throughout the island due to the influence of Drana, and a number of legions have set out to investigate.

One day, Daeva using the dimensional portal to the Abyss began to report highly unusual occurrences. Upon passing through the portal, they would arrive at an unfamiliar location whose existence was entirely unrecorded. The area appeared above the location of a powerful Odyle storm in the lower layer of Reshanta, and so it came to be called Middle Reshanta.

Visitors would report the impossibility of flying, and investigations eventually found that the flow of Odyle in the middle layer was unique: Odyle continuously flowed down from the middle layer to the lower layer. Long flights were easy thanks to the high concentration of Odyle in the lower layer, whereas even spreading one's wings was a challenge in the middle.

This strengthened the Balaur and other hostile forces that were not dependent on Odyle, making them an even greater threat in the middle layer. As a result, the Daeva selected and dispatched are elite combatants striving to eradicate the hostile forces there.
A den of grave robber Daeva obsessed with an relic buried in a tomb. They've set up camp near the cemetery and are causing havoc. They are notorious even among fellow grave robbers.
A bridge that connects northern Altgard to the Moslan Forest. Named by the Nornir after their teacher Munin.
The Mutated Varg Test Subjects were once human, but they no longer remember who they were. All that remains is the command to guard the treasure, a duty they obey without question.

One of many secret locations recently discovered in Atreia, used by the Balaur to store Odylium for study. Odyle Energy fused with souls can be obtained from the Odylium within, which has been distorted and rendered unstable by cruel Balaur experiments.

Once an annex attached to the Eltnen Barrier Tower, this area served as a final refuge for the Life Daeva when the tower collapsed.
In the end, the Balaur stormed the halls, slaughtering nearly all the Daeva hidden within.
Yet, even in the shadow of death, life still blooms. It was here that Kion, the very last of the Life Daeva, was able to ascend.

(Temporary) A once lush land reduced to a vast desert by the loss of Odyle.
Rich in Drana, the sand appears unremarkable during the day, but glows a faint red at night.

A Thieves Camp led by Ugaros.
They are building their own castle with the wealth they have accumulated by looting nearby trading companies and villagers.

(Temporary) A place where Ishtar's favored Taruna Brigade is stationed.
The Red Dragon's Garden is a small stronghold in front of the fortress, abundant with wild Drana.
Due to Odyle anomalies, Sky Islands overgrown with Drana drift above the land.
A self-sustaining village of natives to Morheim. Despite lying on the edge of Nephra Snowfield, it is rather mild thanks to the warm winds blowing from the western coast and southern volcanic region.
A place of the Notos Legionnaires who have been assigned to monitor and deal with the Corrupted Spirits in the lower part of the Canyon.
The Cantas Valley is home to a colony of giant mushrooms that grow higher than the trees. These giant mushrooms greatly favor caves with moist soil and adequate humidity.

In a cave stained with blood and darkness, a tyrant and his followers continue their bizarre rituals.
You must defeat them and rule over forgotten time.

An underground temple located in the center of the Chaotic Middle Reshanta.

In the aftermath of the Last War, the space comprising Reshanta began to warp, causing a number of the floating islands that had been part of the Ancient City of Ru—located on the upper layer of Reshanta—to be sucked downward by the gravitational pull of the Latesran Roots, until they formed a new, middle layer.

This displacement largely destroyed the Underground Temple, resulting in its current exposed state that renders its name somewhat meaningless.
A campsite for explorers of the ruins along the Ellun River Midstream.

This is a gorge connecting the Ishtar castle on the outskirts of Poeta and various areas of Poeta Island.
It is a small, narrow road on the outskirts of the fortress, so there are no people around.
A western camp base located in the southwest of Chaotic Lower Reshanta.
Dawn Legion is the temporary Forward Base built on Poeta Island for the operation to rescue Phernos.

A research facility where countless Gravi are harvested to evolve into Gravarax.
Gravarax are an object of fascination for some Lepharist researchers due to their natural evolutionary processes. By studying Gravarax, these researchers seek to replicate the same mechanisms of evolution in their own test subjects.

An underground repository that was been buried underneath the earth for many years, forgotten, until marauders turned it into a hideout and slaughterhouse.
Defeat the band of ruthless, headhunting ruffians and their leader.
An island isolated far from the rest of Altgard, now made accessible by a recently discovered Windstream. Because it was isolated from Altgard long ago, the island's ecosystem evolved separately.

A village in northern Altgard with a long history.
Having developed over time as a refuge for those fleeing legal troubles or the Balaur, its residents are extremely wary of outsiders.
More recently, a Balaur Dredgion crashed in front of the village, isolating it further from the outside world, but also making it generally safe from Balaur threats.

A ridge separating the Patamor Plains and Nephra Snowfield.
The pass blocks blizzards from traveling beyond the snowfield.
Patamor Village residents and Kromede's followers must pass through here to trade.

A campsite set up in the area of the Floating Temple of Arkanis in order to find the Ascension Artifact.
Kromede's followers are operating under the cloak of secrecy due to the occupation by Sigebert's forces.

Ulgorn, forcibly augmented with Fafnite.

After being gravely injured, he was taken by the Blades and transformed into a test subject for Fafnite augmentation. Stripped of all memories, only unrelenting rage remains.

A base of the Astin Mercenaries, operating in Tolbas Forest. Though comprised only of humans, they pride themselves on skills that they feel put them on par with any company of Daeva. They are often hired by the Wind Breeze Merchants.

A Balaur base set up to monitor the area around Black Claw Village. Watch Captain Amurahta keeps a close eye to ensure the local Mau do their work efficiently, and extorts them for their supplies under the pretext of offering them protection.

A place where the soldiers of the Zumion Temple gathered during the battle against Meslamtaeda and the Balaur. Now destroyed, the area contains only ruins and the roaming, vengeful spirits of ancient Daeva warriors who died in the war. Notos Legionnaires have gathered to investigate the site and keep watch for any threatening spirits.
An outpost established by those dispatched to investigate the Crimson Isle. It serves as a forward base where Creion and other adventurers exploring the Crimson Isle can rest.
A farm along the Ellun River Midstream. Despite its appearance as a peaceful and ordinary farm, its owner, Pamos, is involved in shady dealings with marauders.

A hill named after a legendary Tursin Krall chieftain. Also serving as a path to the Drana Plantation and the Balaur Stronghold, its proximity to these locations means there is a significant risk of encountering Balaur minions.
A campsite located along the Kraka Footpath. It was established to monitor the path leading from Kraka Footpath into Zumion Village.
STR_Subzone_LookoutsRock_Desc Do not use the Collapsed Oracle Subzone
The hideout of Ritualist Amunta who was exiled from Black Claw Village. In the past, there were many crates of supplies for the Daybreak Society, but now they have been looted and are empty.

A wasteland between the Eracus Desert and the Fractured Land.
Nomads used to stay in these lands, but no longer, making the land completely worthless.

A canyon in eastern Verteron. Legend has it that the canyon's intricate and majestic terrain was formed under the influence of Etheria and the Spirit King. The area is monitored closely by the Notos Legion.

A temporary campsite built to facilitate the search for Kochi and the other abducted Shugo. It is located on the forest road to Aullaeu Village, and a Dawn legionnaire has been dispatched to scout the area.

A small rest stop that was originally home to the loggers of Moslan Forest before being taken over by a band of thieves after the forest burned down. The thieves hunt forest creatures or rob refugees who pass through.
A place where criminals exiled even from Safe Haven eke out a living by digging through the debris of the crashed Dredgion for useful items, or fishing relics out of the streams of wastewater.
A cave where a group of Klaw live. It is said that there is a special herb that grows in the Klaw habitat.
Home to an Agrint contaminated by Drana. A valuable treasure is said to lie unattended somewhere inside.
A contaminated land rich with deposits of Fafnite Gemstone.

This newly observed region at the edge of the Abyss has been designated as the 'upper layer'. Investigation suggests that it is composed of fragments from the 'Bloodflame Nebula'. Once a part of the upper Abyss, these fragments were torn away from the nebula and displaced here by the impact of the Second Great Catastrophe.

Observed within the region are remnants of the fortresses Krotan, Dukysas, and La Miren—as well as Ereshkigal’s brigade. The entrance to Reshanta's Eye is yet to be found, however. The central island is overgrown with clusters of thorn trees mutated by Drana and has been dubbed the 'Red Thorn Crown Isle.'

Initial surveys and attempts to access the area have been delayed due to its location at the outer edge of the Abyss, and the presence of a peculiar force field that repels Daeva of considerable strength. This field continues to hinder a full-scale investigation, and some theorize it may be a barrier established to protect a specific target.

Formerly part of the Ferocious Horn Den before it was drawn into the Abyss, this den is now ruled by Gargaum, who has mastered the power of the primal Mau.
Once defeated and exiled by Nuakum, Gargaum returned and subdued his former tribe through his newfound strength.
When the full moon rises, he revels in the hunt, slaughtering even his fellow Mau.

The site of a temple was built to honor Zumion, the first Daeva, when AION was whole and Elysea and Asmodae were one. It was blessed by AION and flourished as a holy place for many years, but fell into ruin after the war.

A deep gorge formed by tectonic shifts.
Suspicious individuals of unknown identity have regularly been seen coming and going.

Once a place for weary travelers to dip their feet in the stream flowing here, now dry.
This is also the location of a stockpile of goods belonging to the Tsenka Merchants in case of attack.
An outpost of a chasing unit of Balaur, tasked with killing experiments that escape from the stronghold or run amok.
A campsite used by the Shulak, until they abandoned it as the Blades increased their presence in the area. It is now home to surviving members of legions destroyed by the Blades.

A tent situated in the north, housing human laborers working in Dranactus. Its fabric is so worn that it hardly suits to keep out the rain. Drugged and delirious laborers either rest in a daze, or collapse while struggling to catch their breath.

This cave is rumored to contain a miraculous cure-all mushroom.
But none who've entered in search of it have ever returned.

Most of the Varg who escaped from the Lepharist Research Center became minions of the Dragon Lords, but some of them scattered and formed their own packs. The Varg who have settled in caves near the Purifying Forest slaughter or capture rare animals in the forest for illegal trade.

The Three Sisters of Fate who lead the Nornir are renowned diviners and prophets. Some of their disciples once claimed to surpass even their teachers in the art of prophecy. But when they foresaw themselves becoming Karas, they hid within this cave in fear, only to meet the very fate they sought to escape.

A secret library built by the librarian Hypatia to preserve the knowledge of the Elyos, under the sworn protection of the Kerubar. Whispers tell of ancient tomes containing information on the Bulwark.
A hill in Altgard where a massive clash between Balaur and defiant Daeva took place. Now it is a peaceful meadow frequented by grazing animals.

A place where Drana trees are grown and harvested for Drana fruit, managed by individuals who have been modified and enhanced by the Balaur, for whom it is a vital food source. In the past, Drana fruit had to be harvested and processed by hand, but devices have since been developed that allow the extraction of energy directly from the Drana tree itself, before being collected in repositories and fed directly into the Balaur Fortress. At the center of the Drana Plantation looms Ishtar's imposing Power Tower.

A hall built by Reda, High Priestess of Illusion, as she wandered the continent searching for her lost daughter.
Seeing her daughter's future reflected in Daeva who had become Sura and specters unable to return to Odyle, she summoned them here.
After obtaining the Mirror of Desire once used by Kromede, Reda used it to sever her obsessive attachment to her daughter from herself and seal it within the hall.

An outpost occupied by the Balaur. A site of fierce battles between Balaur and Davea in the past, following their victory, it is now used by the Balaur as an observation post to monitor the Ellun River Marsh.
A site assumed to be a former part of Zumion Temple. Now little more than broken ruins, perhaps it might contain records of ancient times.

The Forgotten Battlefield is the site of the Eternal Legion's struggle against the Balaur during the raising of the Bulwark by the Empyrean Lords.
You must find <QK>The One Who Remembers Narun</>, a Daeva who fought to the very end before perishing.
Black Fragments Area - Kration Conflict Zone
A region located at the highest altitudes in the center of Lower Reshanta. The atmosphere is unstable due to its proximity to the depths of the Abyss.

An altar where sleepless souls give nightmares as offerings.
Defeat the twisted army of nightmares and the evil spell-cursed horde, and rule over this forbidden realm.

In their darkest hour, a group of Daeva gathered what little they could and sought refuge in a hidden cave behind Basfelt Waterfall. Some ventured out to search for supplies or survivors, but none ever returned. Gripped by fear and despair, those who remained never left their sanctuary, choosing instead to wait in silence as hope slowly faded away.
The Revelations of Khalil foretell the fate of the Daeva. A fragment of this ancient prophecy is said to lie hidden within this Rock Cave, guarded by the Kalgolem.

A base set up by the Tsenka Merchants where Shugo who purify and transport water are staying.
Supplies are regularly sent here from the Tsenka Merchants' Village, but attacks by marauders are causing trouble.
A cave used for mass burial of those killed by Meslamtaeda's poison. After consuming the contaminated corpses, the Targos inside have mutated and taken over the cave for themselves.

A temporary trading post for the Steel Hammer Merchants, located south of Idun's Lake. Established to facilitate trade between Amunta and Popokiki, it enjoys a prime location on the route connecting Southern and Eastern Gribade, but is modest in terms of scale.
Archipelago of Siel's Wings - Siel's Right Wing

The forward base of Dignuaka, the 62nd Unit Commander of the Ishtar Taruna Brigade.
During a routine patrol, Digunaka was impressed by the highly efficient Drana energy the Lepharists created, and has been using the energy to evolve and surpass his own limits.

An outpost of elite Balaur forces monitoring and patrolling Dranactus. They oversee Drana cultivation while keeping watch over the area. A teleportation device allows them to rapidly reinforce their forces, making this a key base.
A cave of violent outcasts that banded together after the Balaur emerged. Lately, their aggression has extended to Daeva, as well as the Balaur.
This place was called the Pilgrim's Ridge Path because it was a must-stop for those visiting the Zumion Temple and the Ardus Shrine.
A small base for a group of people who make their living searching for and stealing relics from the Basfelt Ruins. It consists of a barely more than a few mud huts and stacked chests of looted goods.

A temporary base for Kromede, back when she was still active in Morheim. Abandoned ever since Kromede claimed the Sky Island as her base, it is now occupied by servants of Fafnir bewitched by the Domination Stone.
A canyon in northern Altgard. There are various minerals and caves located along the north of the canyon.

A grotto hidden along Mahindel River, currently used as a laboratory by the Creion—a research organization formed by Lepharists trying to find an alternative energy source to Odyle. They have conducted various studies in this pursuit and also invented many things, including the Selvis.
A floating island located in the very center of Chaotic Middle Reshanta.
Headquarters of the Wind Breeze Merchants, who trade mainly in Verteron. The Shugo of the Wind Breeze Merchants settled here as they set a high value on the Biruta leaves grow in Tolbas Forest.

Atheron chose to build his secret research base in "Deus", where the vast storms that assault the Abyss are born.
Inside, he hid a clone of himself, and put the facility under the strict management of his loyal subordinate, Laboratory Chief Nazmun.

After the destruction of the Abyss Gate of Verteron Fortress, some of the Klaw that lived in the Abyss have settled in the Verteron Fortress Ruins. The Klaw queen, Karat, spawns from her nest and seeks to expand their territory.

A citadel built by the Daeva to withstand the Balaur invasion. Constructed in the mountains, it was ideally positioned for defense. However, when the Balaur assault swept over it like a storm, the citadel stood on the brink of collapse. As a last resort, the Daeva commander resorted to dark magic and narrowly succeeded in driving back the Balaur—but at the cost of their corrupted souls and fallen honor. Now, having lost their purpose, they continue to guard the citadel in the hope that an honorable death will allow them to return to the Aether.
The elevated areas of the western highlands and canyon region surrounding Zumion Village. Rock Tomb Hill and vast grasslands stretch across the area.
A small campsite built in the northern Tranein Highland. Avent, Nemon's loyal subordinate, resides here to watch over the Tranein Lake area.

This is where the stone statues of Uruthum and the eleven Daevas who defeated Minusha were erected. Currently, the site is in ruins as several statues are missing and the structure has deteriorated over time.

Zumion, the first Daeva, was granted relics and a temple of her own by AION.
Envious of this, Dragon Lord Meslamtaeda invaded and destroyed the temple, turning the priests within to stone.
No one knows if any safe place may be left in the once-submerged temple.
A temporary base built to investigate the area around the Dredgion Crash Site. Dispatched Daeva are keeping an eye on this area and are carrying out the tasks given by Nemon.

The village of the Black Claw Tribe, Mau minions of the Balaur. As soon as the Black Claw Tribe experienced the power of Fafnite, they disavowed their ancestors and swore allegiance to the Balaur in pursuit of ever-greater power.

A form of abyss that lives inside Arch Daeva, created through Asahr's power.
Sigebert's abyss manifests to reveal her inner darkness and greed.

A plantation for Drana built by the Balaur. These plantations can be found all across Elysea, as Drana are able to develop unique characteristics depending on their environment. The vegetation in this specific area is known to cause mutations in Drana.
Once the stronghold of a legion known as the Golden Branch Brigade. Now, it is occupied by a group of thieves stealing hard-earned Odyle found by refugees at the destroyed Eltnen Barrier Tower.

A once-sacred land where the Temple of Life stood and a great oasis blessed by the power of Yustiel flowed with clear water.
After the fall of Eltnen and the disappearance of the Life Daeva, Mystic Spring grew contaminated and Drana covered the area.
Later, the Lepharists emerged to occupy the area, turning the Mystic Spring of Anathe and Temple of Life into their main strongholds.

An outpost established by the Balaur outside the Sanctum Outpost. Though disguised as a simple outpost, it is actually a facility for testing Draconute modification, with many violent Draconutes who have slipped beyond Drakan control.

An Elim village at the entrance to Moslan Forest founded under the leadership of Odar, an Elim elder. A recent attack by the Blood Blades resulted in the Elim Odar falling into a deep sleep, and the Nornir in the village being abducted.

A research facility packed with the Lepharists' most fanatical and aggressive special operations units. Driven by an obsession with strength, these radicals willingly become test subjects for their own experiments, fostering an atmosphere of ruthless competition in the name of enhancing combat performance.

Once an altar to Kaisinel visited by numerous worshippers and guarded by a spirit summoned by the High Priestess of Illusion, after the High Priestess abandoned her duties, it was sealed and became no more than a ruin. But the spirit still guards it, waiting for its mistress to return.
An area where the Drana harvested from the Drana Cultivation Area is transported or processed. There are a lot of pipelines and repositories that branch out from the power conversion unit.

A cave located in the Contaminated Marsh, polluted by the sewage and refuse of Nahid Brigade Fortress and the Drana Plantation. Hidden among the waste are a number of documents detailing the Balaur's Surana experiments.
Formerly a Legion outpost overseeing the Muspel Volcano Zone, it fell into ruin following a volcanic eruption. It now serves as the base of a cult that worships the volcano.

A former camp for lumberjacks and hunters from the days when the Patamor Plains were still a forest. Long abandoned, it was rumored to have been resettled by outsiders. Now, only their ghosts roam the site, alongside fearless outlaws who have turned the haunted camp into their base of operations.

A barracks once used by the Destruction Archons, followers of the Empyrean Lord of Destruction, until it was destroyed by the Balaur and left in its current state.
Blaming themselves for their failure to protect their Empyrean Lord, the Archons became Apparitions after death and now attack all who enter their sanctuary.

This storage room is where the Balaur imprison Daeva to extract Fafnite from them. It is said to hold not only stores of Fafnium, but also Balaur records detailing the creation and properties of both Fafnite and Fafnium.

A form of abyss that lives inside Arch Daeva, created through Asahr's power.
Chloris's abyss manifests to reveal her inner torment and sadness.
A Draconute battalion is being temporarily stationed here to keep an eye on the Calderon Canyon.
A mysterious cave shrouded in mystery. There is a legend that Daeva sought it out in the past for ascension.

A subspace of distorted time and space, where forgotten fates are sealed away.
You must eliminate those who guard chaos and redirect the flow of these fates.
A breeding ground where the Black Claw Mau raise their fearsome Tayga. The grounds are forever filled with the scent of blood and the savage howls of these beasts.
A base for members of the Daybreak Society fleeing Black Claw Village. It was once a sacred place to the Mau because of the grave of their great hero, Zemurru, but no one visits anymore.

A tent situated in the east, housing human laborers working in Dranactus. Its fabric is so worn that it hardly suits to keep out the rain. Drugged and delirious laborers either rest in a daze, or collapse while struggling to catch their breath.
A land of the dead, on the outskirts of the continent.
A campsite located on the edge of the Southern Altamia Highland, where Notos Legion guards are stationed.

A giant whale that once roamed the skies, now little more than a corpse exploited by the Balaur for resources.
Defeat the main forces at the base to cut off the Balaur's resource supply.

The Fire Temple was once a sight of pilgrimage for Ancient Daeva, where they gave their relics as offerings. Kromede, the fallen Silent Judicator and passionate treasure hunter, infiltrated the Fire Temple with her eyes set on these relics, only to be consumed by the Mirror of Desire. Ever since, Desire given shape in the form of Kromede has continued to tempt those who visit the Temple.

A cave occupied by Naga who reluctantly follow Sigebert's command in the absence of their leader, Dragon Lord Fafnir. They share frosty relations with the Fate Archons, and consider the Krall to be beneath them.

A temple so ancient that its origins are lost to time. Gradually flooded by seawater over eons, most of the structure and the valuables within now lie buried underwater. However, whispers persist of treasure waiting in areas yet to be swallowed by the sea.

The enforcer of the Blades.
Armed with a giant scythe, he is incredibly loyal and prefers to brutally execute traitors personally. He lives to fight, especially to the death.
A cave where a passage to the unstable Abyss has appeared. It contains information about the Ancient City of Ru.

A village formed by Daeva and humans fleeing the Balaur, and home base of the Notos Legion. It is located within ancient ruins hidden in Altamia Canyon, and was once submerged underwater alongside the Zumion Temple, only to reemerge when the topography of Altamia Canyon changed due to wars between Elyos, Asmodians, and Balaur.
An outpost of the Balaur scouts patrolling the Altamia Canyon area. A number of innocent residents of Altamia Canyon are imprisoned inside in terrible conditions.

A molten lake formed by the lava that flows in from Muspel Volcano.
The swirling lava creates a colossal vortex that threatens to swallow the valley whole. Stories say that a famous hot spring once existed here long ago, but the truth of these claims remains unknown.
Deep within this cave, Zikel’s zealots carry out grim rituals, driven by a warped devotion. The remains of their victims are gathered and laid before them as offerings, presented as tribute to Zikel.

A mutated <QK>Varg</> that has grown immensely in both size and ferocity. Portions of its body have mineralized into armor-like plating, making it even more formidable. Any lingering trace of its humanity has long since vanished, leaving it a mindless, uncontrollable beast incapable of communication. It tears through its foes with massive, mineralized claws.
A <QK>northern camp</> base located in the south of Chaotic Upper Reshanta.

The location of the Eltnen Barrier Tower and its fortress.
The Eltnen Barrier Tower was a central defensive location for important areas in Eltnen, making it a primary target for Ishtar during the invasion. After the barrier was destroyed by the Balaur's concentrated fire, the tower and fortress were so thoroughly annihilated that barely a trace remains but for the site itself.
A contaminated marsh downstream of the Ellun River flowing through Verteron, now uninhabitable due to the wastewater from the Balaur's Drana Plantation.

The upper eastern area of Gribade Highland—no more than a parched land with only a small patch of grass. A temporary campsite has been built by a Black Claw search party sent to capture Amunta and members of the Daybreak Society.
A street stall of Shulak located on the road to Morheim. It sells goods from Morheim or medicines that can only be found in the southernmost part of Altgard.
A cave once filled with clean groundwater, now tainted by the contaminated Mystic Spring. With the fresh water cut off, all it attracts is creatures who thrive on its filth.

The grudges of the countless killed by their hands continued to torment the Balaur even after death, latching to the very stonework of the fortress until the Balaur were forced to abandon it.
Hordes of undead swarmed the abandoned fortress to the point it began affect the surrounding area.
They must be dealt with before they grow too powerful.

A recently excavated cave archive that was hidden from the world for a long time. Likely built to store records detailing the construction of the Eiron Hill ruins nearby, its interior is now too deteriorated to yield any useful data.
Today, all that remains is the wandering spirits of the Life Daeva who once managed the archive.

The laboratory of Atheron, the head of the Lepharists in Elysea, who intends to become a god.
He is continuing research on his clones in order to become a perfect being and expects that the Ascension Artifact will provide the missing piece needed to complete his magnum opus.
A cave used by those who seek the power of the Balaur over the honor of the Mau. Here, the followers of Shaman Kumbahum continue to grow in strength.
A marsh downstream of the Ellun River that flows through Verteron. There was once a Verteron Barrier Tower, but it was destroyed by the Balaur.

Yet another research facility established by Atheron within the unstable Abyss known as Deus.
Once Atheron realized that the Abyss storms hindered the Balaur's access to Deus, he built a series of secret laboratories throughout the region. Within each one, he sought to reach godhood by creating the experimental being known as Atiel.

The Atiel created in this particular facility had been the most promising to Atheron. However, its exceptionally strong sense of self caused it to turn hostile during the experiment and attack Atheron himself. Enraged that the research center was partially destroyed and consumed by the unstable Abyss storms, Atheron shut down the entire facility—and his failure along with it.

The sealed research center is now overseen by Gromkas under Atheron's orders. Meanwhile, Zylus, the facility's former research director, remains trapped inside with his own creation, consumed by madness.
A cave not often visited by the villagers of Aullaeu in Tolbas Forest. It seems to be the site of suspicious trade.

A former hideout and home to the Nornir who protected the forest, until their souls were stolen during an attack by the Blades. Now in ruins, the hideout is filled with the vengeful wraiths driven mad by despair.

One of the outposts closest to Kromede's Island and near the Fire Temple.
In front is the Fire Temple, behind is swirling lava, and heat all around.
Strictly managed under Kromede's orders, the movements of the Fire Temple are closely monitored here.

An outpost now held by the Flauke Legion. Once protectors of the Purifying Forest, they became deeply demoralized after suffering a brutal defeat to the Balaur. Driven by the power of Fafnite, Commander Flauke is now guilty of innumerous atrocities.

The warden of the Dranactus Underkeep.

Narcissistic and merciless, he takes pleasure in inflicting pain upon others, reveling in the suffering he causes.

A cave created to shield the Fire Temple from the humid ocean air. For eons, the Spirit guarding it remained faithful to an ancient promise made with Kromede—only to be consumed by wrath after rumors that she abandoned the temple and fled.

A band of thieves settled in the Pilgrim's Ridge. Their main targets are the residents of Zumion Village and pilgrims traveling to and from there. In addition to robbing pilgrims of their goods, they are also known to enjoy kidnap and blackmail.

A bird summoned by the Aullaeu shamans of the Urugugu tribe through the borrowed power of Dragon Lord Ishtar.

Believed to embody the essence of the Aullaeu, these birds serve as their protectors.

An Aullaeu sorcery pattern is inscribed upon their chests.
A training base for Fate Archons under Sigebert's command. What looks like an unassuming cave from the outside actually houses an elaborate fortress full of security devices meant to deter intruders.

A labor training facility where Cogni under Balaur command are trained to be laborers.
Kobold, Dracuni, and Balaur live together in this space.
<Caretaker Sinandash> is assigned as the captain of the training facility.
An area of floating rocks or remains of fortresses destroyed in the Last War. It is the closest area to the eastern camp base and is relatively easy to access from the base by gliding.
Base in Front of the Supply Depot

Not even noble blood could save you from the plague that spread after Odyle was depleted. Behit, the last surviving heir of a noble house that remained outside the Bulwark, buried his family with his own hands after they became Karas. He then entered the Abandoned Grave and sealed himself within.
An altar where the Naga Wasti performs sacred rites to bolster the Dragon Lord's power. Renowned as a formidable warrior, Wasti is feared across the land as the Daeva Slayer.

Once the tomb of an ancient nameless Daeva, this place was later transformed into a place where the Karas were imprisoned and killed. 
When the Balaur invasion began, those with nowhere else to run fled to the crypt, sealing the doors by sacrificing some of their own. But none returned, and none survived.
An area filled with dangerous creatures that have adapted to the thick sulfur contaminating the swamp.
A storage housing the Blades' Odylium marauders. Fortified with powerful security devices, it holds vital documents tied to Odylium.
A twisted pit believed to descend into the Ancient City of Ru, known only to the most daring explorers. Rumors persist that the lost records of Ru are hidden within its depths.

An artificial cave created by Fire Temple worshipers. Much care went into maintaining the cave, as the Guardian statues were relocated in an attempt to counteract Water Aura from the ocean. Now, however, it lies abandoned.
A base built with the remnants of the old ruins, located at the entrance to Uruthumheim from Moslan Forest.
A cave located deep in the Tolbas Forest. The cave is inhabited by highly poisonous plants and animals, making it difficult to access.
A Fafnite Gemstone Mine located in the Gribade Highland. The Steel Hammer Merchants, who obtained the mining rights from the Balaur, are using their laborers to dig for Fafnite Gemstones.
An area consisting of the main island in the south (Left Wing of Siel, Heart of Siel, and Right Wing of Siel) and the secondary island in the north (Grave of Steel).
The northern of two floating islands bearing the scars of a Dredgion crash.

A hiding place storing items stolen by fugitives from Lacephin Village. The stash contains a variety of items, including a book on magic—which was used by one of the fugitives to seal the storage door.
A steep cliff area located on the outskirts of Ishalgen. The terrain is rugged, the land empty, with no traces of any inhabitants.
The creation of Fafnite always requires a living human or Daeva. To ensure a constant supply of sacrifices, the Drakan Homish constructed this prison compound to confine both humans and Daeva.
A <QK>western camp</> base located in the west of Chaotic Middle Reshanta.

A group of thieves based in Western Gribade Highland. Originally, they preyed on nearby refugees, but now they cooperate with the Blades, handing over to them any suspicious outsiders passing through.

An island in Etheria under the rule of Boulder Lord Vakron and guarded by his spirits.
This island became the stronghold of Vakron after he crossed into Atreia to punish the spirits of Atreia who refused the call of the Spirit Realm.
Once an ordinary floating island, it now exudes a mystical aura and teems with empowered flora and mutated creatures shaped by the energy of the Spirit Realm.

A small base of the Wind Breeze Merchants near the Verteron Fortress Ruins.
Rumor has it that a Shugo named Dundu also trades with the Krall.

According to legend, the Ancient City of Ru was once the pinnacle of Atreian civilization, until it was consumed by the Abyss and vanished without a trace. For generations, its fate remained a mystery, with only scattered fragments of the once-magnificent city ever discovered in Reshanta.

By tracing the unique wavelength of Ru's Heart, a relic from the lost city, the relentless relic hunters of the Shuliman Expedition uncovered the ruins of Ru and the shifting Abyss connected to them. News of the discovery quickly spread, drawing adventurers from across Atreia in search of the rumored relic of Israphel. However, the entrance to the shifting Abyss proved costly to maintain and was often forced to close.

To this day, uncovering the secrets hidden within Ru remains the lifelong ambition of countless adventurers.

A gathering place for deserters from the Illusion Cavaliers. The despair caused by the destruction of the Illusion Cavaliers caused many to abandon their pride as Daeva and leave the fortress. Now they are harsh and cruel, unrecognizable as the Cavaliers they once were.

A facility where the Balaur imprison experimental subjects for post-experiment monitoring. Those who underwent mutation and those still retaining human form are confined together, creating a tense atmosphere.
A hidden base at the canyon where refugees from all over Altgard gather. The food supply is poor, so empty bellies abound.

A mutated Karas discovered in the Crypt.
Once an ordinary Daeva, Heladrir infiltrated the Crypt to find his crush <QK>Giselle</>, who had been buried within following a false accusation of being Karas. Heladrir never found his beloved, and instead fell victim to the enraged Karas inside. Over the years, Heladrir mutated into a Karas himself, losing all humanity save for the memory of his affection for Giselle.

A graveyard established during an age when countless humans and Daeva perished each day. The immense number of souls interred here, most denied even the dignity of a name, has turned it into a place few dare approach. Yet as rumors of buried treasures continue to spread, an increasing number of grave robbers have begun to take notice.

An outpost manned by Balaur of the Lagta Brigade, built to support their research into destroying the Blood Barrier. Whether human or Shulak, any who dare approach Impetusium Square without permission are attacked indiscriminately.

An officer of the Lagta Brigade under Fafnir's command.

As captain of a Dredgion, he travels far and wide harvesting Fafnite. Driven by an insatiable thirst for power, Rathman augmented his body with Fafnite, causing two blade-like growths to emerge from his arms.

Those who cling to twisted beliefs about Zikel gather within this chamber of repentance. These fanatics claim to be his most devoted followers, yet their misguided zeal has only deepened the misconceptions surrounding his true nature.

A post made by Patamor Village residents to monitor the Balaur.
This is the last holdout for villagers to fight back against the Balaur invasion.

This area connects Fafnir's fortress with various regions of Ishalgen.
It is a small, narrow road on the outskirts of the fortress, so there are no people around.

A tent situated in the south, housing human laborers working in Dranactus. Its fabric is so worn that it hardly suits to keep out the rain. Drugged and delirious laborers either rest in a daze, or collapse while struggling to catch their breath.

A cave located along the coastal cliffs of the Western Cantas Valley, a region once rich in Odylium.
It is rarely visited due to rumors of Sura being discovered inside.
At some point, a mysterious barrier appeared at the cave entrance.

A camp where hunters from Patamor Village stay while away for longer periods.
Also used by villagers to hide from the Balaur.
A granary used by the residents of Verteron until Dratona forces turned it into a Balaur lair. The Dratona captain, Nagto, has wasted no time in pocketing the accumulated grain.
A Balaur storage that holds Drana, Drana by-products, and the supplies needed to grow Drana.

A manifestation of Zumion's Relic, the Warding Feather, taking human form within the Zumion Relic Storage.
